findings.what_happened: The PECO breakdown for the candidate question 'association between grades and sleep' had Exposure = Grades, Comparison = 'Less or no grades', Outcome = Sleep. This reverses my idea (sleep affecting grades) and the comparison is meaningless. I only spotted it because I opened 'Full reasoning'. I fixed it by hand. A first-year would not know PECO well enough to catch it, and the chosen question would have gone into the report.
findings.expected: Exposure and outcome match the question's direction, and the comparison is a sensible contrast (for example 'adequate sleep').
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the PECO fields from the same parse as the question wording. Add a validation that Exposure and Outcome appear in the question in the right order. Show the PECO breakdown next to the question on the card, not only inside the collapsed reasoning.

findings.what_happened: Quote chips for quality questions show a green 'found word for word' tick even when the quote does not answer the question. For example 'Follow-up complete and long enough' is backed by 'FUNDING: Ministry of Health, Singapore.', and 'Cohort clearly defined' is backed by the paper's own title. The caveat 'found means the words are in the paper, not that they prove the answer' is only in grey text above the list. A newcomer reads a green tick as 'verified'. The first appraised paper was also an economic modelling study judged against a 'cohort study' checklist.
findings.expected: A tick means the quote supports the answer, or the badge wording makes clear it only means the text exists. A paper's appraisal checklist matches its design.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the badge to 'quote exists in the text' or add a separate 'supports the answer?' check. Warn when the quote is only the title or funding line. Pick the checklist from the paper's detected design.

findings.what_happened: In demo mode nothing about the final question is grounded in sleep or grades. The sleep topic matched 0 papers and the three appraised papers were about diabetic eye screening, telehealth literacy and an HIV app. The synthesis 'Known' statements say only '(mock) 2 key findings were extracted for this topic', and the 'Unknown' statements say only '(mock) Gaps signalled by the studies' own limitations'. Gap statements for my sleep and grades question cite 'Triana et al. 2020'. The demo banner and the '(mock)' labels are honest, but the finished review cannot be shown to a tutor, and I could not judge whether the real workflow would produce useful synthesis text.
findings.expected: Either a demo that matches a plausible topic, or an explicit end-of-run statement that no statement in this review can be used. Synthesis statements should have real content tied to their quotes.
findings.suggested_fix: In demo mode, add a recorded sample set for common student topics such as sleep and grades. Make the synthesis mock statements quote-specific. Add a 'not usable as a real review' reminder on the export step, not only in the report header.

findings.page: Step 3 / Step 6 consequence: topics with no matching papers
findings.what_happened: Ranking ended with Sleep and Academic performance at 0 papers selected and only 3 papers in total. The checklist item 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic' was ticked as done while the warning said 4 topics had fewer than 3 papers. The ranking table's top rows said 'does not match the topic' next to scores of 58 and 54, and they were not selected. A confirm dialog did catch the problem, which was good, but I had no obvious recovery path other than 'Appraise anyway'.
findings.expected: A contradictory tick is not shown. The user is told clearly how to recover, for example by editing the topic or search words.
findings.suggested_fix: Tick 'Keep 3-5 per topic' only when it is true. In the dialog, offer 'Edit searches (step 3)' as a button alongside 'Go back' and 'Appraise anyway'. Explain what 'does not match the topic' means next to a score.

findings.what_happened: The automatic search topics were a poor reading of my answers. 'Whether people' was created as a topic from my sentence 'Whether people who sleep less get lower grades'. The 'Who' field kept my whole answer, including 'I'm not sure about age'. Sleep, my main topic, started with 0 synonyms and 0 MeSH. Topic edits were also easy to lose: 'Delete' appears on every row, I could not tell which row would be hit, and Sleep disappeared with no undo or confirmation (Ctrl+Z did nothing). The step also reads 'Aim for 4-8 topics. You have 3.'
findings.expected: Short, sensible noun-phrase topics. A visible undo, or a confirm, when deleting a topic.
findings.suggested_fix: Trim the answers into noun phrases before making topics. Show an 'Undo' toast after deleting a topic. Give each Delete button an accessible name that includes the topic, for example 'Delete Sleep'.

findings.what_happened: The step uses unexplained jargon: 'Controlled vocabulary (MeSH)', '0 MeSH', 'title/abstract', 'Query', 'Count matches', 'group 1: any of ... AND group 2'. The topic cards show 'Done' while the step panel says 'Not started'. The query for 'Grades' shows 'grades, grade AND Sleep', so the topic name is merged with another topic's words. Counts of 7,629 or 9,245 papers look authoritative, although the banner explains they are recorded samples.
findings.expected: Plain-language labels, or a one-line gloss for MeSH. Status words that agree across card and panel.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one-line plain explanations for MeSH and 'title/abstract' as help text. Use 'Search' rather than 'Query'. Align the status labels between the card and the panel.

findings.what_happened: After typing my idea on the New review page, the canvas asked me again 'Tell us what you want to research' (step 1 of 9) with the same text pre-filled and a 'Start scoping' button. The idea card still said 'Your turn / Draft idea' while the active step was Scoping. I wondered whether my first entry had been lost. 'Canvas' and 'List' toggles are unexplained. The List view was much clearer to me than the Canvas.
findings.expected: Step 1 counts as done once I typed my idea, or the step is a clear confirm step. List view is perhaps the default for newcomers.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip or merge step 1 when the idea was already entered. Alternatively say 'Check your idea' and name the card 'Your idea: approve to continue'. Consider defaulting to List view for first-time users.

findings.what_happened: On the sign-up page the password hint ('At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email.') is drawn on top of the password input and overlaps the field's border. Keyboard focus starts in Email, so the optional name field is skipped. The 'Create account' button looks active while the helper reports it as disabled until the fields are filled.
findings.expected: Hint below the field, not overlapping. A disabled button looks disabled, or stays enabled and validates on submit.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the hint into normal flow below the input. Style the disabled state, or validate on submit.

findings.what_happened: Study type and article type filters work and are easy to find. The colours plus shapes in the legend are readable and consistent between table, map and chart. However, the legend does not say what each study type means (no gloss such as 'Cross-sectional: a snapshot survey'), and it does not explain the difference between 'Review article 12' and 'Systematic / scoping review 8'. Selecting one chip from each row gave 'Showing 5 of 96' (an intersection) and nothing said 'AND'. Cohort (orange square) and Qualitative (amber diamond) are close in hue. The 3D plot says 'Height has no meaning yet', which looks unfinished. Step 4 says 79 papers are 'Not reported' while step 5 says 16, with only a one-line explanation.
findings.expected: A first-timer can tell what each category means without outside knowledge, and understands how two filters combine.
findings.suggested_fix: Add hover or tooltip glosses for each study type, using the meanings table. Write 'Showing 5 of 96 that are BOTH ...'. Remove 'Height has no meaning yet' or give height a meaning. Separate the cohort and qualitative hues further.

findings.what_happened: Demo scripting leaks into the user-facing text: 'Paraphrase presented as a quote — should be flagged' and 'deliberately altered' appear beside the not-found quotes, and the synthesis has a '(mock) sample conflict ... paired at random'. These are honest but make the review feel staged. Jargon such as PICo and PECO, 'quality questions for a cohort study', 'Rejected quotes are left out of the synthesis', 'Markdown' and 'BibTeX' is only partly glossed. The chosen question title still shows '(mock)' until edited. The export lists 'Markdown, plain text with formatting marks such as # for headings', which would put a first-year off.
findings.expected: Plain wording a first-year understands, with a 'what this means' line. A flagged-demo label that does not read like a test script.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip internal annotations from the demo text. Add short glosses for PECO, PICo, BibTeX and Markdown. Default to the printable report for people who want to read it, and keep Markdown as secondary.

findings.what_happened: After I edited the chosen question to 'Do university students who sleep less get lower grades?', the report still carried the old '(mock) Sample gap', '(mock) Feasible with an online survey of about 300 people' and the novelty check run for the old question wording, listing telemedicine papers as 'what was found'. The novelty section is correctly worded 'not proof of novelty', but the edit did not mark the gap, feasibility or novelty check as out of date.
findings.expected: Editing the question flags the gap, feasibility and novelty check as needing a re-run, or re-runs them.
findings.suggested_fix: After a question edit, show an 'out of date' badge on the gap, feasibility and novelty items. Offer 'Re-run novelty check' next to the Save button.

findings.what_happened: The progress text is inconsistent: '1 of 5 questions' next to '5 more to cover' (6 in total). Only 5 questions were asked, so 'which kinds of studies' was never asked and showed 'not answered yet'. 'Rank the papers' is the label, the panel is called 'Summary & ranking', and the page header says 'Table'. The My projects card keeps the raw first sentence as its title even after a question is chosen.
findings.expected: Consistent counts and names. The project title or subtitle shows the chosen research question.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the counter arithmetic. Ask about study types within the five questions, or drop it from the 'what we know' list. Show the chosen question as the project subtitle.

three_second_test.note: The page is for turning a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. I would click 'Start a review' first, then sign up. The 9-steps-in-3-stages cards make the whole journey clear. The animated demo further down is dark and slow, and the first thing in it ('How do health systems in South...') is unrelated to my topic.
Page for making an account. I would type email and password, then click Create account. The password hint overlaps the field.
Page for typing my idea in a sentence or two. I would write my sentence or click an example chip, then click 'Start my review'. Very clear and reassuring ('does not need to be polished').

A dark canvas with one card and a 9-step strip. I would click 'Open step 1', but I did not understand why my idea was being asked for again, and what the card 'Your turn' / 'Sharpen my idea' meant versus the blue button.
The page is for answering short questions about my idea. I would type an answer, then press 'Send answer'. The 'What we know so far' box helped, and 'Skip the rest' was reassuring.

Page for keeping or deleting suggested topics. I would click 'Keep' on the ones I like, then 'Keep N suggested topics'. The identical Keep and Delete buttons on every row made me worry about clicking the wrong one.

I understood this turns topics into database searches, and that I click 'Write the searches' then 'Run all 8 searches'. I did not understand 'MeSH', 'controlled vocabulary', or the AND/group logic. A cautious student would just press the big button.
Page showing how many papers were found and how many were duplicates. I would read the big numbers, then click 'Summarise the papers'. The article-type and study-type bars were useful.
Page for skimming papers and fixing wrong cells. I would tick through the 3-item checklist, then 'Rank the papers'. Filter chips with shapes and counts were easy to use.
A warning about fewer than 3 papers and topics with 0 selected. I understood something was wrong, but not what I could do about it, and a checklist tick contradicted the warning.

Dense: quality checklists, AI answers, quotes, ticks and a 'show only quotes I need to decide' option. I understood I had to decide the red 'not found' quotes and then click 'Summarise the evidence', but I could not tell why a funding line counted as evidence.
Known / contested / unknown per topic, with quote chips. I would read each tab, then click 'Suggest research questions'. The statements themselves were empty placeholders.
Three candidate questions with gap, feasibility and weakness on each card. I would compare them, click 'Choose this question', then 'Finish and export'. Very clear.

The page says my review is ready. I would check the question and click 'Download the report (Markdown)'. The format names (Markdown, CSV, BibTeX) were confusing but the printable-report option helped.

reports.categories_and_colours: Found and filtered by study type and by article type in the Step 4 retrieval mix, and in the Step 5 and Step 6 tables and maps, via two rows of chips with counts (Study type: Trial, Cohort / case-control, Cross-sectional, Qualitative / mixed methods, Systematic / scoping review, Other design, Not reported; Article type: Journal article, Review article, Preprint, Editorial / letter / comment, Other publication). Filtering was easy. Clicking a chip shows 'Showing X of Y: ...', says how many papers are hidden and keeps 'Reset filters' visible. The map and chart legends use colour plus shape plus a label: blue circle = Trial, orange square = Cohort, green triangle = Cross-sectional, amber diamond = Qualitative / mixed methods, pink star = Systematic / scoping review, green cross = Other design, grey ring = Not reported. I understood that colour and shape show the kind of study and that clicking a legend item isolates it, because the legend text says 'hover or focus to highlight, click to show only that category'. It did not say what each study type means. Study type counts differ between step 4 (79 Not reported) and step 5 (16), which is explained only in one line. Two filters from different rows combined as AND without saying so (5 of 96). Cohort and Qualitative have similar orange and amber hues. Counts in the legends matched the bars. The 3D plot note 'Height has no meaning yet' looks unfinished.
reports.validity_assessment: Traceability is good. Every quote can be opened with 'Show source' and is highlighted in the retrieved abstract. Altered quotes are flagged 'not found, you decide' with the closest passage and a 54% word match, and I could reject them with an undo. Papers come with real DOIs and abstracts. The report header states 'Demo: scripted AI and recorded sample papers; not a real review', says a found quote 'shows the words are in the paper, not that they prove the claim', and labels the novelty check 'what was found, not proof of novelty'. The question step says 'Finding none does not prove a question is new'. I found no calling the question 'novel'. Weaknesses: (1) the green 'found word for word' tick can sit on quotes irrelevant to the quality question (title, funding line); (2) the PECO fields for my chosen candidate were reversed and nonsensical (Exposure = Grades, Outcome = Sleep); (3) in demo mode the three appraised papers, the synthesis statements and the gap text have nothing to do with sleep and grades, so I could not tell whether the real workflow gives a usable synthesis; (4) editing the question did not mark gap, feasibility and novelty check as out of date; (5) an inconsistent 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic' tick while 4 topics had fewer than 3 papers. Overall: honest about being a demo and the evidence trail is real, but the output is not something I could show my tutor, and I would not know that the PECO error needed fixing.
reports.would_have_quit_at: Step 6 Ranking. The screen told me 'Fewer than 3 papers selected in 4 topics', two of my topics had 0 papers, and the top-scored papers said 'does not match the topic'. As an anxious first-year I would worry I had done something wrong, with no clear way to fix it except 'Appraise anyway'. I only kept going because the task asked me to finish. The next-worst point was Step 7, where the checklists and quotes felt too technical, and the papers were unrelated to my topic.
reports.activity: Created one account (Mai, mai.undergrad.qa2@example.com) and one project ('I'm interested in sleep and grades', id prj_c4a4f211227c40ae). Answered 5 scoping questions, kept 4 topics (I accidentally deleted the suggested Sleep topic, removed 'Whether people', and added Sleep and Academic performance by hand), ran 8 searches (96 unique papers from 136), generated summaries (10 of 10 batches) and ranking, appraised 3 papers, rejected 3 altered quotes, generated synthesis and 3 candidate questions, chose candidate 2 and edited its wording and PECO fields, finished the export and clicked 'Download the report (Markdown)'. The app showed 'Downloading the report', and I did not open the file. I could not open the printable report in a new view with the helper (the click did not change the visible URL). No console errors or failed requests were reported by the problems command at any step. About 105 helper commands used.
reports.narrative: I landed on Athena feeling nervous, but the headline and the nine steps in three stages made sense straight away, so I signed up. The password hint sat on top of the password box, which looked sloppy. Typing my vague idea felt safe, and then the canvas asked for the same idea again, which confused me. The scoping questions were friendly and let me say 'I'm not sure'. The suggested topics included a nonsense one ('Whether people'), and when I clicked Delete I lost Sleep, my main topic, with no undo. The search step threw MeSH and 'controlled vocabulary' at me, so I just pressed the big button. The demo banner told me the papers are about telemedicine, which I appreciated, but it meant every later step felt unreal. The retrieval and table pages were my favourite part: the chips with shapes and counts made filtering by study type and article type easy. Ranking worried me, because Sleep had no papers and a tick said I was fine while a warning said I was not. In appraisal I liked being able to open a source quote and see it highlighted, and I rejected the altered quotes. But a green tick on a funding line as 'evidence' made me trust the ticks less. The synthesis was empty placeholders. The three candidate questions were clear, but when I opened the reasoning I saw sleep and grades swapped round, so I edited it. Export was straightforward, though 'Markdown' and 'BibTeX' meant nothing to me. I finished, but I would not show this to my tutor.

findings.page: Step 9 Research question: Full reasoning and quotes (candidate 2)
findings.what_happened: The gap for my question is backed by green-ticked chips ('Tran et al. 2025 · limitation' and two more). Clicking one shows a verbatim quote about healthcare/veterinary data-sharing in rural areas, which has nothing to do with mindfulness or burnout. It carries a 'found word for word' badge. The gap sentence ('the included papers do not measure this link directly') is vacuously true because none of the papers are about the topic. The report repeats these citations as support for the gap.
findings.expected: A traceable claim should be backed by a quote that is relevant to it. At minimum, the tick should not read as 'verified' when the quote does not support the statement, and the app should say when the evidence base is off-topic.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a relevance signal next to 'found word for word', for example 'relevance to this statement: low' or a topic-match flag. Warn on the question card when fewer than N selected papers match the question's topics. Make the checkmark wording say 'quote exists' rather than a tick that looks like approval.

findings.what_happened: After 'Summarise without them' the progress strip jumped to step 8, but the side panel stayed on 'Viewing step 7 of 9 · Appraisal · Done'. Its primary button was still 'Next paper', which is the wrong action. The new Synthesis card on the canvas sat half hidden behind the panel. I had to find 'Suggest research questions' on that card. Clicking it created step 9 directly. I never saw the synthesis (known/contested/unknown) that the landing page promises. Earlier steps advanced the panel automatically, so this one is inconsistent.
findings.expected: The panel moves to step 8 (synthesis) or offers 'Go to step 8', as ux-intent.md says. The user reads known, contested and unknown before questions are suggested.
findings.suggested_fix: When the current step advances, switch the panel to the new current step. If the panel is showing an earlier step, make the footer primary 'Go to step N'. Do not let 'Suggest research questions' skip an unread synthesis without a prompt.

findings.what_happened: The 'Before you continue' checklist shows 'Keep 3–5 papers per topic' struck through as Done (1 of 3 done). The orange warning below it says three topics have fewer than 3 papers, and my core topic, Burnout, has 0 selected. The checklist and the warning contradict each other.
findings.expected: The item stays open or shows a warning state while topics are under-covered.
findings.suggested_fix: Tick that checklist item only when every topic has at least 3 selected papers, or reword it to 'Review the selection'.

findings.what_happened: The checklist quotes do not line up with the questions. For 'Comprehensive search of multiple databases' the AI says Unclear and quotes a sentence about digital transformation. The quote about ProQuest, Semantic Scholar and PubMed is attached to 'Risk of bias'. On the canvas card, '✓ 70 ✗ 9' has no labels. The panel says '9 quotes to decide' across 8 papers and gives no sense of how long that takes. I decided one and skipped 8.
findings.expected: Quotes sit under the question they answer. Counts say what they count.
findings.suggested_fix: Check quote-to-question relevance in the mock and in real runs. Label the card counts ('70 quotes found, 9 to decide'). Add an estimated time for the quote decisions.

findings.page: Step 4 Retrieval and Step 9 novelty check
findings.what_happened: The match counts do not agree with each other. The Burnout, ICU nurses and Measurement queries all show 'PubMed 8,058'. The Mindfulness query shows 'PubMed 38'. The novelty check later reports 'pubmed: 7629 hits' for the mindfulness AND burnout query, while its top results are telemedicine papers.
findings.expected: Counts are consistent and plausible, or labelled as sample numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Label every demo count as 'sample', or generate consistent fake counts. In real mode, show the query behind each count.

findings.what_happened: The password hint ('At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email.') is drawn over the bottom of the password field, so the dots and the hint overlap and the field looks cut off. The two text lines also touch the button area.
findings.expected: The hint sits below the field with its own space.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the hint outside the input's box (margin-top, or aria-describedby with a block element below the input).

findings.what_happened: The headline of the 'What we know so far' block reads 'questions done' with the count missing. The collapsed section reads '1 questions'. The canvas card still says 'Idea · Your turn' while step 1 is ticked as Approved.
findings.expected: '1 of 5 questions done' / '1 question'. Card status matches the step strip.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the pluralisation and the empty count. Update the Idea card status once step 1 is approved.

findings.what_happened: On the canvas after I typed my idea, the next-step banner said 'Tell us what you want to research' and 'Open step 1', which I had already done. The card had a second button, 'Sharpen my idea'. Then the first scoping question asked 'Who do you want to study?' while the side block already said 'Who: ICU nurses'. An impatient user wonders what the app did with their sentence.
findings.expected: After I submit my idea, the app moves on to the first question that is actually new. The banner does not repeat step 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Banner says 'Next: answer a few questions to sharpen it'. If the app already has the answer, pre-fill it ('ICU nurses, correct?') or skip it.

findings.what_happened: Topic cards show 'Done' while the step panel says 'Not started'. The field 'Controlled vocabulary (MeSH)' shows 'none' and cards say '0 MeSH' with no explanation of what MeSH is or whether empty is fine. The query blocks use 'group 1: any of', 'title/abstract' and 'AND', which are dense for a hurried reader.
findings.expected: Status words agree. One line says what MeSH is and that it is optional.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a hint such as 'MeSH = PubMed's official subject headings. Optional; Athena adds them in real mode.' Use 'Topic ready' rather than 'Done' for topics.

findings.page: Step 5 Table and Step 6 Ranking (study type labels)
findings.what_happened: The 'Trial' study type (blue circle, '6') is mostly protocols and registrations with no results. Five of the six rows are protocols. Their key findings are junk like '(mock) NCT07198828.' A narrative literature review ('Digital health in Indonesia: A literature review') is labelled 'Qualitative / mixed methods'. A user could read 'Trial 6' as six trials with outcome evidence.
findings.expected: Protocols are not counted as trials with results, and a review is not labelled qualitative.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Protocol' sub-label or filter (the sub-label already exists in the row, so show it on the chip). Do not use an NCT number as a 'key finding'; fall back to the abstract's results sentence or show 'no results reported'.

findings.what_happened: Article-type and study-type counts are both shown, and the legend pairs colour with shape and count, which is good. But (a) 124 of 136 papers are grey 'Not reported' rings, so the chart says little before the AI runs. (b) Clicking an article type changes the chart that sits below the fold, so I saw only a text message and not the effect. (c) 'Depth: topic' and 'Height has no meaning yet' make the 3D scatter hard to read. (d) In the table, 'Review article 13' and 'Systematic / scoping review 11' look like the same thing with no explanation of the difference.
findings.expected: A first-time user can say what the colours and shapes mean and see the effect of a filter right where they click.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the chart above the bars or sticky. After a filter click, scroll the chart into view or show a mini-count inside the chip. Add a one-line tooltip: 'Article type = what kind of publication; study type = how the research was done'.

findings.what_happened: The default report format is Markdown, described as 'plain text with formatting marks such as # for headings'. A nursing student wants Word or PDF. 'Open printable report' appeared to do nothing in my browser (URL and page unchanged, probably a new tab I could not see). 'Download Markdown' gave no on-page confirmation. 'Larger preview' is not larger: it is a small scroll box showing 200 of 553 lines.
findings.expected: One clear 'Download report (Word/PDF)' path and a visible confirmation after clicking.
findings.suggested_fix: Offer .docx or PDF as the primary report download. Show 'Downloaded: filename' after a click, and say when a link opens in a new tab. Make the larger preview full-page.

findings.what_happened: After I clicked 'Rank the papers' on the table page, the ranking page opened already scrolled down mid-table. The headline 'Check which papers go forward' and the warning were out of view. I thought the step had not changed until I scrolled up.
findings.expected: A new step opens at the top of the page.
findings.suggested_fix: Scroll to top whenever the step changes.

findings.what_happened: The 'Create account' and 'Start my review' buttons are fully coloured even while the page reports them as disabled (empty form). A user cannot tell they are inactive. The step-1 helper text 'Write at least a sentence to start' is small and grey.
findings.expected: Disabled buttons look disabled, or the form validates on submit with a visible message.
findings.suggested_fix: Give disabled primaries a muted style, or keep them enabled and show an inline error on click.

findings.what_happened: The side panel covers about 60 percent of the canvas. The nodes it asks me to act on (suggested topic cards with Accept / Dismiss) are cut off at the panel edge.
findings.expected: The canvas re-centres the active node in the visible area.
findings.suggested_fix: Pan the canvas to centre the active node in the remaining space when the panel opens.

findings.what_happened: The landing page does not mention that this is a demo. I only learned it after sign-up from the banner. '(mock)' is part of the research question text and the report, so a student who copies the exported question into a proposal copies '(mock)' too.
findings.expected: The landing page says early that this is a demo, or the page gives it up front as a free trial with sample data. Mock markers are stripped or clearly separated from the question text.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Demo mode: sample papers' to the landing page when the server is in demo mode. Render '(mock)' as a badge, not part of the question string.

findings.what_happened: I tabbed through the synthesis panel: focus outlines were visible on 'More actions' and 'Close panel'. 'problems' reported no console errors or failed requests at any step.
findings.expected: Visible focus and no errors.
findings.suggested_fix: None. This is a positive note.

three_second_test.note: Tool turns an idea into a research question using real papers. I would click 'Start a review'. Nothing mentioned demo mode.
Create an account. The password hint overlaps the password field.
Type the idea, click 'Start my review'. Example chips are helpful.
One card and a banner saying 'Tell us what you want to research' after I had typed it. Two buttons ('Open step 1' and 'Sharpen my idea') made me unsure which was right.
The app asks about my topic. 'Skip the rest' is easy to find. The question repeated what I had already said.
Click 'Suggest search topics'. Copy glitches ('1 questions', 'questions done').
Keep the suggested topics with one big button.
Click 'Write the searches', then 'Run all 8 searches'. MeSH and 'group 1: any of' were unexplained jargon.
136 papers found, 44 duplicates; click 'Summarise the papers'. The chart and legend took longer to understand.
Sparse panel: counts and a button to open the table. I could not tell what the table would look like until I opened it.
Filters by study type and article type are obvious; colours, shapes and counts are clear.
Landed scrolled down mid-table, so the headline was out of view. After scrolling up the orange warning was clear.
A lot of text: checklist, AI answers and quotes. The 'found word for word' explainer helped, but it took more than 3 seconds.
The panel still said Step 7 with 'Next paper' as the main button after step 8 had started.
Three candidates with gap, feasibility and weakness; click 'Choose this question'. 'Finish and export' is locked until I choose.
The review is ready to download. Markdown means nothing to me; I wanted Word or PDF.

reports.categories_and_colours: Study type has seven categories, each with a colour and a shape: Trial = blue circle, Cohort/case-control = orange square, Cross-sectional = green triangle, Qualitative/mixed = amber diamond, Systematic/scoping review = pink star, Other design = green cross, Not reported = grey ring. The legend is always shown with counts (zero-count categories are dimmed), and it is repeated in the retrieval chart key, the filter chips and the table cells. The same shape and colour appear everywhere I looked (chip, table cell, chart key). Article type (Journal article, Review article, Preprint, Editorial/letter/comment, Other) uses plain ink bars and no hue. I could filter by both in the retrieval step (article type affects the chart) and in the table (both chip rows work). The messages are honest: 'Showing 6 of 136: trial. 130 papers are hidden by your filters (still in the review)' with a 'Reset filters' button. Retrieval-step study-type counts (124 'Not reported') change to the AI-read counts in the table (17 'Not reported'), and the page explains why. What confused me: (1) article type vs study type are two similar rows with no explanation of the difference ('Review article 13' vs 'Systematic / scoping review 11'); (2) 'Trial' includes protocols that have no results; (3) the 3D chart's 'Depth: topic' and 'Height has no meaning' are hard to read, so I used the table instead; (4) the chart sits below the fold, so I could not see the effect of an article-type click; (5) green appears twice (cross for Other design, triangle for Cross-sectional), distinguishable only by shape, though the shapes did separate them. Green ticks ('found word for word') use the same green idea as 'good', which risks being read as 'verified'.
reports.validity_assessment: Honesty about the demo is strong and consistent: a dismissible banner on every page says the AI is scripted and papers are recorded samples about telemedicine in Southeast Asia, '(mock)' marks AI text, the search builder says 'these searches are a recorded example, not built from your topics', and the report opens with 'Demo: scripted AI and recorded sample papers; not a real review', 'Generated by Athena prototype', and quote statistics (70 found, 9 not found, 1 rejected by me, 8 undecided). The quote check is real traceability: I saw a deliberately altered quote flagged in red ('not found, you decide') with Accept anyway / Reject / Undo, and rejected quotes were left out of the synthesis and counted in the report. The novelty section carries the caveat 'Finding none does not prove a question is new' and the report says 'not proof of novelty'. Nothing was called 'novel'. Warnings were honest: the ranking step said my Burnout topic had 0 papers and the dialog said topics would have 'little or no evidence'. Weaknesses that threaten a valid, traceable review: (1) 'found word for word' only proves the words exist, not that they support the claim. The gap for Candidate 2 was supported by green-ticked quotes about healthcare/veterinary data-sharing, unrelated to mindfulness or burnout, so a hurried student could cite an unsupported gap. (2) The 'gap' wording is vacuous when the papers are off-topic. (3) The app let me go from 0 Burnout papers to a chosen question and a full report with only one warning dialog; nothing blocks or flags the final report as built on irrelevant evidence beyond the demo banner. (4) Candidate questions downgrade 'effect' to 'association' (a cross-sectional survey), and none is an intervention or trial design for an 'effect of interventions' topic. (5) The synthesis step was skipped past without being shown, so a user could reach a question without reading what the evidence says. (6) Counts are inconsistent (PubMed 8,058 for three topics, 38 for one, 7,629 in the novelty check). (7) Study-type labels can mislead (protocols counted as 'Trial', a literature review labelled qualitative). I found nothing that looked fabricated beyond what the demo discloses, but in real mode the relevance of quotes to claims needs a check. For my dissertation proposal in two days I could not use this output as is: the papers are about telemedicine.

reports.narrative: I'm Daniel, my proposal is due in two days, and I want my question and my report with as few clicks as possible. The landing page is clear: idea in, research question out. I click Start a review and sign up. The password hint sits on top of the field, which is a little odd, but I'm through. I type my topic, click Start, and land on a canvas with one card and a banner telling me to tell it what I want to research, which I just did. I click Sharpen my idea, get asked who I want to study although it already shows ICU nurses, and click Skip the rest. Then I need another click to get topics. Fine. I keep all four topics, write the searches, and run all eight. The demo banner tells me the papers are about telemedicine. That's honest, but it makes me wonder what I'm doing here. Retrieval finds 136 papers. The colour key is good: shapes plus counts, and clicking filters. The table filters work well. Ranking is where I get nervous: my Burnout topic has zero papers. I click Appraise anyway. Appraisal is dense. I find one altered quote flagged in red, reject it, and skip the rest. Then the panel gets stuck on step 7 with a Next paper button and I have to hunt for Suggest research questions on a half-hidden card. I choose the association question, click a supporting quote, and see a healthcare/veterinary sentence under a green tick, which doesn't support a mindfulness gap at all. Export is only Markdown, which I can't open in Word. I preview the report, which says clearly that it's a demo. I'd not use this for my proposal, but the flow is solid.

findings.page: Step 3 Search builder and Step 4 Retrieval
findings.what_happened: Counts do not reconcile. My edited PubMed query was counted as 8,058 matches, but the retrieval run then listed 'Long COVID PubMed 979' and fetched 0 papers from it. The per-search table also shows 'Healthcare workers' and 'Doctors' returning identical hits (979 PubMed / 1,630 OpenAlex). The demo banner says edits are ignored, but nothing on the retrieval page repeats that, and nothing flags a search that fetched 0.
findings.expected: The count shown before running should match the count after running. A search that fetched 0 papers should be flagged, and the retrieval page should restate that the numbers are recorded samples.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a warning on the retrieval page when a query fetched 0 papers or when the pre-run count differs from the run count. Repeat the demo caveat next to the hit counts there. Do not reuse the same recorded count for different topics without saying so.

findings.what_happened: Each topic becomes its own query of the form 'this topic AND return-to-work outcomes'. There is no combined query joining population AND exposure AND outcome, so the final corpus is a union of five partial searches. The MeSH term and two of the six synonyms I entered (long-haul COVID, post-COVID syndrome) were left out of the generated PubMed text. They appear only as copy-chips under 'Keywords you can add'. Clicking a chip gave no visible confirmation that it had copied. My own manual edit was correctly parsed into labelled groups ('edited by you'), which I liked.
findings.expected: A defensible search joins population, exposure and outcome blocks and includes every synonym and MeSH term the user entered. Anything left out should be stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Offer an 'all topics combined' query as the default. Auto-include the user's MeSH terms and synonyms, or say plainly which were omitted and why. Show a 'copied' confirmation on the chips.

findings.what_happened: Only the top 40 or so papers per search were collected: 275 results fetched against thousands of hits. The page does warn 'only the 40 most relevant will be collected', and the report has a hits/fetched table. But nothing says this is not an exhaustive systematic search. The report has no PRISMA-style flow, no screening log, and no reasons for excluding the 127 papers that were not selected. All screening is by AI score plus one reviewer.
findings.expected: For a committee-defensible review, the report states its limits: not exhaustive, single reviewer, AI-ranked screening. It also gives identified, screened, excluded and included counts with reasons.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Limits of this method' paragraph and a PRISMA-style flow summary (identified, deduplicated, selected, appraised) to the report, with exclusion reasons or an explicit 'not recorded'.

findings.what_happened: The 'Before you continue' checklist marks 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic' as done (ticked, struck through). The amber banner directly below says fewer than 3 papers are selected in 2 topics: Long COVID has 0 and Return-to-work has 1. The checklist contradicts the warning.
findings.expected: The checklist should show that item as not done, or as a warning, while the banner says the condition is unmet.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the checklist item from the same rule as the banner (every topic has 3-5 selected) and show it as unticked or amber while any topic fails.

findings.what_happened: The novelty check for the question reported 8,058 PubMed and 1,630 OpenAlex matches for 'long COVID AND return-to-work'. The card still presents 'Gap it fills' and cites telemedicine papers (Noceda 2023, Sabrina 2021, Ayob 2025) as support. The novelty query ignores the healthcare-worker population. Its top hits are all papers 'already in your review', about telemedicine. A large match count is not interpreted at all. The caveat 'finding none does not prove it is new' covers the opposite case, not finding thousands.
findings.expected: Thousands of near matches should trigger an explicit 'this area is well studied; your gap may not be novel' message. Gap claims should be grounded in papers that are actually on topic.
findings.suggested_fix: Show an interpretation next to the novelty counts (for example 'many matches: narrow your question before claiming a gap'). Include the population block in the novelty query. Refuse to cite quotes from papers that failed the topic match as gap evidence.

findings.what_happened: The Long COVID topic had 0 matching papers and is silently absent from the synthesis tabs. There is no 'no evidence found for this topic' statement. Known statements are vacuous ('(mock) 8 key findings were extracted'). The 'Contested' statement reuses the same two quotes as 'Known'. All three candidate questions shrink the population to 'doctors', dropping the nurses and allied health I specified. Candidate 3, 'What helps or hinders long COVID among doctors?', is not a coherent research question.
findings.expected: A topic with no evidence should be listed as an explicit gap. Contested statements should cite opposing quotes. Candidate questions should keep the user's stated population.
findings.suggested_fix: Render every approved topic in the synthesis, with 'No papers matched' where applicable. Require conflicts to cite quotes from at least two different papers. Build candidates from the scoping answers so the population is not narrowed without saying so.

findings.what_happened: In the Markdown preview the DOI of one paper shows as 'shb.shb160_24' with part of it in italics, because the underscores were parsed as emphasis. The BibTeX preview has the correct DOI '10.4103/shb.shb_160_24'. A mangled DOI in the report undermines traceability.
findings.expected: DOIs render exactly as in the source record, in the report and in the printable version.
findings.suggested_fix: Escape underscores in DOIs, or put DOIs in code spans or links, in the Markdown and the rendered preview.

findings.page: Step 9 Edit this question and Export
findings.what_happened: After I rewrote the question as a 12-month sustained-return question and changed the population, the 'Gap it fills', feasibility, weakness, supporting quotes and Design ('Cross-sectional survey') all stayed as generated for the original wording. A cross-sectional survey cannot answer a 'within 12 months' question. There was no prompt to re-run the novelty check. The report prints them as if they belonged to my edited question.
findings.expected: Editing the question marks the dependent fields as out of date and offers to refresh them. At minimum the design/question mismatch is flagged.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark gap, feasibility, design and novelty as 'based on the earlier wording' after an edit, and offer 'Re-run for my wording'.

findings.what_happened: Ranking says '13 selected' but the Appraisal step shows '12 papers' and the export says 'Papers appraised 12'. The missing paper is never named. I had swapped one paper earlier, which may be related.
findings.expected: The selected count equals the appraised count, or the difference is explained.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain the drop (for example, no abstract or text) and list excluded selections in the appraisal summary.

findings.expected: Title keeps a usable width and headers do not overlap. The table scrolls horizontally if it needs more space.

findings.what_happened: The password hint ('At least 10 characters...') is rendered on top of the password input box, so the hint text overlaps the field's bottom edge. The Create account button looked disabled in the page summary although it worked.

findings.what_happened: The first scoping question, 'Who do you want to study?', repeated what my idea already said (healthcare workers). The study-types question was never asked: 'Which kinds of studies' stayed 'not answered yet' after 'questions done'. The report then recorded 'studyTypes: (mock) Any design', which I never said. The Add button in 'Add or merge topics' did not add my topic on the first click. Pressing Enter in the name field worked.
findings.expected: Skip questions already answered. If a scoping field is unanswered, the report should say 'not specified', not invent 'Any design'. The Add button should work.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not ask for facts already extracted. Record unanswered scoping fields as 'not specified'. Check the Add button handler.

findings.what_happened: 'Key finding' cells hold abstract sentences cut mid-sentence ('...sustainable digital transformation in') or just a trial registry number ('(mock) NCT07198828.'). The label implies a result that is not there. Correcting a cell works and is tagged 'edited by you', but the edit committed only on Tab (Enter left the box open with no hint). The 'edited by you' badge also appeared under Study type although I changed only Key finding.
findings.expected: Key finding shows a result statement or 'no result reported'. The edit-commit gesture is explained, and the badge is per cell.
findings.suggested_fix: Trim at sentence boundaries, detect registry-ID-only text, add 'Enter to save, Esc to cancel' under the editor, and scope the 'edited' badge to the changed cell.

findings.what_happened: After 'Summarise without them', the step strip moved to step 8 but the panel stayed on Appraisal ('Viewing step 7 of 9'). I had to find and click the Synthesis node myself. Earlier steps advanced the panel automatically.

findings.what_happened: The question-wording textarea has no accessible name; the helper could not target it by label and the focus report showed an empty name. The other fields (Population, Interest and so on) have only unlabelled text inputs showing the current value.

findings.what_happened: The page says 'Fetched' per search but the headline gives 275 fetched / 140 unique against hits in the thousands, and the filters I set (2020 onward) are visibly ignored: the chart plots papers from 2015. The demo caveat is only on the Step 3 panel. 'Not reported' study type is 130 here but 15 after the AI summary; the page explains this, so it is only a mild surprise.

three_second_test.note: For: guided literature review that ends in a research question. First: read the 3 stages. Next: Start a review. The headline and the two buttons were clear. 'What Athena will not do' is a good trust cue, but it sits below the fold under an auto-playing demo.
For: creating an account. First: fill the fields. Next: Create account. The password hint overlapping the input is distracting.
For: typing my idea. First: write a sentence. Next: Start my review. The example chips and the 'Next:' line made it unmistakable.
A dark canvas with one node, a banner and two similar buttons. I guessed I should open step 1 or click 'Sharpen my idea'. It took longer than 3 seconds to see that they are the same thing.
For: answering a few questions. First: type an answer. Next: Send answer. The 'What we know so far' panel was a good touch.
For: keeping or deleting search topics. First: Keep or Edit each. Next: Use these topics. Dashed suggested cards plus 'suggested' tags were clear.

For: checking the searches before they run. First: read group 1 and group 2. Next: Count matches, then Run all searches. The 'group 1: any of / AND group 2' wording was readable even for a non-librarian.

For: seeing what was found. The headline '275 fetched, 135 duplicates, 140 papers' reads clearly, but the 979/707/8,058 hit counts versus 275 fetched did not reconcile in my head. Next: Summarise the papers.
For: skimming and fixing AI cells. First: click a study-type chip. Next: Rank the papers. The 3-item checklist and the 'AI - abstract' badge were very clear.
For: choosing which papers go forward. The ticked 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic' item contradicted the amber warning below it, so I did not trust the page at a glance.

For: checking AI quality answers against quotes. First: read a paper's checklist and any red 'not found'. Next: Next paper, then Summarise the evidence. The explanation 'found does not mean it proves the answer' was reassuring.
For: reading known, contested and unknown. The structure is clear, but the content ('(mock) 8 key findings were extracted') gave me nothing to read or check. The Next action was clear.
For: choosing one of three questions. First: compare gap, feasibility and weakness. Next: Choose this question, then Finish and export.
For: downloading the review. First: check my question. Next: Download. Three formats are clearly described, and the first line of the report says it is a demo.

reports.categories_and_colours: I could find and filter by both dimensions. Study type has 7 categories, each with a hue, a shape and a count: Trial (blue circle), Cohort/case-control (orange square), Cross-sectional (green triangle), Qualitative/mixed methods (amber diamond), Systematic/scoping review (pink star), Other design (green cross) and Not reported (grey ring). Article type (Journal article, Review article, Preprint, Editorial/letter/comment) is a separate row of plain grey chips with no hues, as the app intends. Both are available as chips in the Summary table and Ranking table, as bars in Retrieval, and as the Colour-by and legend on the 3D map and the 2D chart. Group by also offers study type, article type, topic, source database, year and full text. I understood the study-type meaning from the legend alone. The legend key says 'hover or focus to highlight, click to show only that category'. Clicking Cross-sectional plus Review article combined as AND and gave 'Showing 0 of 140' with a clear 'hidden by your filters (still in the review)' note and a Reset link. That is honest, though the chip counts do not update to show that combination. The Retrieval page says 'Study type (only where the database labels it)', with 130 of 140 as Not reported, and explains that the AI reads abstracts next. That was accurate: after summarising, Not reported fell to 15. Small oddities: Cross-sectional and Other design are both greens and differ mainly by shape. Legend entries with zero papers (Cohort, Cross-sectional, Qualitative at retrieval) are shown dimmed without a '0'. The 3D map's height axis 'has no meaning yet', which the page says plainly.
reports.validity_assessment:
Traceability is the app's strongest feature, and it is mostly honest about the demo. Every appraisal quote is checked word for word and shows its closest source passage. A 'not found' quote gets a similarity percentage and 'Accept anyway' or 'Reject' buttons, and undecided quotes are excluded with a warning. Abstract-only papers are labelled, and 'found does not mean it proves the answer' is stated. The ranking rubric is visible per paper (topic fit, design strength, setting, recency and citation impact, each with its formula), and a swap is recorded as 'changed by you'. The search text is editable and my edit was parsed back into labelled groups. The report opens with 'Demo: scripted AI and recorded sample papers; not a real review.', logs the search table with edit flags, hits and fetched counts, and the BibTeX is clean. The novelty box says that finding nothing is not proof of novelty.

It is not yet a review I could defend to a committee, even setting the demo content aside. (1) The search is per-topic and truncated to roughly 40 papers per query, with no combined population-exposure-outcome query. The MeSH terms and some synonyms I entered were not applied automatically. (2) Pre-run counts and run counts disagree, and an edited query fetched 0 papers with no flag. (3) There is no PRISMA flow, exclusion reasons or limits statement; screening is AI-scored with one reviewer. (4) The synthesis silently drops a topic with 0 papers, and its statements are placeholders. (5) The research-question gap and novelty claims are supported by off-topic papers, and 8,058 matching records are not interpreted. (6) Editing the question does not refresh its dependent fields (gap, feasibility, design). (7) The 13-selected versus 12-appraised discrepancy is unexplained.

On overclaiming: 'novel' is not asserted, and the caveats are present. The residual risk is that the phrase 'Gap it fills' reads as a finding. With the real AI and databases, items 1, 2, 5 and 6 would be the ones to fix first.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I did not quit. The first point where a real rigorous user would hesitate is Step 3, when the generated PubMed query ignores the MeSH term and synonyms they just entered and splits the question into separate topic queries. They would likely quit trusting the review at Step 9, when the novelty check shows 8,058 matches for the exact topic yet the card still presents a 'gap it fills' backed by telemedicine papers.

The report header says "Demo: scripted AI and recorded sample papers; not a real review" and counts quotes (found 119, not found 12, rejected by you 12). The novelty caveat is present: "Finding none does not prove a question is new". The app never claims novelty.

Weaknesses (partly demo artefacts, but a real user would be misled):
(a) The review content has nothing to do with hip fracture or rehabilitation (Singapore mHealth, Indonesian COVID apps). The "Known" statement is only "(mock) 8 key findings were extracted for this topic", and the "Contested" one is a labelled sample conflict "paired at random ... not necessarily disagree".
(b) The novelty check reports 2,207 PubMed hits for "tele-rehabilitation AND hip fracture surgery" but lists "Precision medicine in Thailand" as the #1 hit. The count and the papers contradict each other.
(c) The three candidate questions are all qualitative or associational (experience, association, barriers). None asks the physician's actual question, whether it helps, as an intervention (PICO) question. Candidate 2 reads "association between tele-rehabilitation and hip fracture surgery among adults over 65 after hip fracture surgery".
(d) The same planted fake quote ("clearly proves the intervention works everywhere", "deliberately altered") appears on all 12 papers, and the not-found box says "(mock) Paraphrase presented as a quote — should be flagged" in front of the user. "Accept anyway" sits right beside Reject, which makes it easy to accept an unverified quote.
(e) Some "key finding" cells are not findings (a bibliographic citation string, or "Clinical trials.gov, NCT03117842").
(f) Quote "found word for word" is correctly caveated as "not that they prove the answer".
(g) The chosen question keeps the "(mock)" prefix in the report, so it cannot be forwarded as is.
The workflow would produce a traceable review if the data were real, but this demo cannot show that the app produces a valid one.
reports.narrative: I landed on a dark page that said "Turn a rough idea into a research question you can back up with real papers", and I knew within 3 seconds to tap Start a review. Sign-up was short, though the password hint sat on top of the password box. I typed my hip-fracture tele-rehabilitation question. The next screen asked "Tell us what you want to research" with my idea already filled in, so I felt I was being asked twice. The demo banner reassured me it was scripted, but also told me the papers would be about Southeast Asian telemedicine, so I expected junk. Scoping was easy and "Skip the rest" saved me time. Topics were clear: Keep, Edit, Delete. I liked the "4 more to cover" count, but it stayed stale after I answered. Searches ran in a few seconds and the "135 fetched, 51 duplicates, 84 papers" sentence was a good plain summary. I also liked the colour and shape chips that filtered the table, and the "Showing 2 of 84" line. Ranking warned me that Hip fracture surgery had no papers, which I appreciated. Appraisal was the heaviest part. I had to reject one fake quote on each of 12 papers, and scrolling inside a panel on a phone was fiddly. The synthesis was empty filler ("8 key findings were extracted"), but quote chips opened the real sentence. The three candidate questions did not ask whether tele-rehab works, and the novelty check listed an unrelated Thai paper. I picked candidate 3 and reached export. Download Markdown gave no sign that anything happened. I can't email a .md file from my phone, and the printable report did not open for me. In a real session I'd have quit here.
