findings.what_happened: The question 'Does it help?' was turned into three candidates that are all qualitative or associational: experiences, 'association between tele-rehabilitation and hip fracture surgery among adults over 65 after hip fracture surgery', and barriers and enablers. None is an effectiveness (PICO) question. Candidate 2 repeats itself. The chosen question keeps a '(mock)' prefix in the final report.
findings.expected: At least one candidate that matches the user's intent (an intervention or outcome comparison), grammatical wording, and a clearly labelled demo placeholder that does not read as a real finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the scripted candidates reflect the user's wording and include one comparative or effectiveness question. In real mode, ensure the PICO/PECO phrasing does not repeat the population. Strip '(mock)' only if the report states demo status elsewhere, which it already does.

findings.what_happened: The novelty check reports 2,207 PubMed matches for 'tele-rehabilitation AND hip fracture surgery', and the #1 hit is 'Precision medicine in Thailand (2019)'. The count and the papers shown contradict each other. The text says the search is a fresh database search.
findings.expected: Hits that are plausibly related to the query, or a clear note that in demo mode the listed papers are unrelated sample records.
findings.suggested_fix: In demo mode label the novelty hits as unrelated samples next to the count, or suppress the count. In real mode, do not present the top hits unless they match.

findings.what_happened: I wanted a report I could email to myself from a phone. The main download is a Markdown file ('plain text with formatting marks such as # for headings'). Tapping Download Markdown gave no toast, progress or confirmation. 'Open printable report' (the readable version, which can be saved as PDF) did not visibly change the page. There is no email, share or copy-link option. The first-time Markdown explanation is jargon.
findings.expected: A readable format by default (PDF or web page), clear feedback that a file was saved, and a way to send or share it from a phone.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the printable report/PDF the first choice for the report. Show a confirmation after download ('Saved review.md'). Add Share or Email me this report. Open the printable page in the same tab or tell the user it opens in a new one.

findings.what_happened: Every one of the 12 papers carries the same planted fake quote. The unverified quote box reads '(mock) Paraphrase presented as a quote — should be flagged ... deliberately altered' and 'which clearly proves the intervention works everywhere'. Rejecting needs one tap per paper (12 times), and 'Accept anyway' sits next to Reject with similar weight.
findings.expected: Fewer, varied examples in demo mode, a bulk action (Reject all not-found), and the risky action given less prominence than the safe one.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Reject all not-found quotes on this paper/all papers'. Style 'Accept anyway' as a secondary or confirm-required action. Do not show developer notes ('should be flagged') to users.

findings.what_happened: The Known / Contested / Unknown statements are placeholders: '(mock) 8 key findings were extracted for this topic', '(mock) sample conflict ... paired at random ... not necessarily disagree', 'Gaps signalled by the studies' own limitations'. The three topic tabs cannot give a clinician anything to decide on. The chip labels 'Narvaez 2024 · finding 2' do not say what the finding is until tapped.
findings.expected: Statements that summarise the finding in words, with the quote chip as evidence, or a clear 'demo placeholder' state.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a short quote preview on each chip. In demo mode say plainly that this step shows the layout only. In real mode, the Known statements need actual content.

findings.what_happened: A 2-page editorial ('Technology Literacy as a Barrier to Telehealth During COVID-19') is labelled 'Systematic / scoping review' with a citation string as its key finding. Two protocols are labelled 'Trial' (they have no results) and the key finding is just 'Clinical trials.gov, NCT03117842'. The paper detail says 'Randomised trial' while the chip says 'Trial'.
findings.expected: Study-type labels that match the paper, protocols flagged as protocols, and key findings that are findings.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Protocol' category or flag. Reject registry IDs and bibliographic strings as key findings. Use the same name for a category everywhere.

findings.what_happened: The retrieval step shows Study type 'Not reported 73' (database labels only) and the table step shows 'Not reported 14' (after AI). Only a small grey line explains the difference. 'Review article 12' (article type) and 'Systematic / scoping review 8' (study type) overlap in meaning without explanation.
findings.expected: A short explanation of the two groupings that moves with the numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Put 'before AI reading' and 'after AI reading' next to the numbers, and a one-line 'article type is how it was published; study type is how it was done'.

findings.what_happened: On the sign-up form the password hint ('At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email.') is drawn inside the password input box and overlaps the field.
findings.expected: The hint sits below the field.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the hint's positioning so it sits under the input and does not overlap it.

findings.what_happened: After typing my idea on /s/new, I land on a list with 'Tell us what you want to research' and an 'Open step 1' button. Opening it shows my idea already typed and asks for 'Start scoping'. I felt I was asked twice. The 'What happens in this step 8 s' label is unclear.
findings.expected: Skip straight to the scoping questions, or tell me my idea is saved and the next click is scoping.
findings.suggested_fix: Move directly into scoping, or reword step 1 as 'Your idea is saved. Check it, then continue'. Say '8-second video' instead of '8 s'.

findings.what_happened: On a phone the 2D chart dots are tiny (about 4 px), and Edit/Delete links on topics are small tap targets. Panel scroll was fiddly: some actions needed the page focused before keys scrolled the panel, and screenshots showed only the top of the panel. The 'Open printable report' link shows no visible focus style.
findings.expected: Thumb-friendly targets (44 px) and a clear scroll area.
findings.suggested_fix: Enlarge tap areas and offer a tappable list fallback to the dots. Add a visible focus style. Make the panel the scroll container for touch.

findings.what_happened: The checklist item 'Keep 3–5 papers per topic' is ticked done while Hip fracture surgery has 0 papers selected and a warning says fewer than 3 are selected for it. The 'Appraise selected papers' button stays enabled and the interstitial must be cleared.
findings.expected: Checklist reflects the warning (not done).
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the checklist item done only when every topic has at least 3 selected papers.

findings.what_happened: After answering a scoping question, the line '4 more to cover: where, what you want to know...' stays unchanged. It still lists the same topics after the second question. 'Search topics taking shape' only shows 3 topics and 'Measurement and outcomes' appears later with no explanation.
findings.expected: The counts and list update after each answer.
findings.suggested_fix: Recompute the 'still to cover' list after each answer.

findings.what_happened: On a phone the canvas opens panned to the far right, with only the 'Questions' and 'Export' nodes partly cropped. There is no clear way to see the whole map without hunting for zoom controls. List view is better, but the Canvas toggle is the first option.
findings.expected: The canvas fits the whole review or defaults to the list on phones.
findings.suggested_fix: Default to List on narrow screens, or auto-fit the canvas.

findings.what_happened: The 'See a review take shape' video is illustrated with tiny text that cannot be read at 375 px. The landing page says nothing about demo mode up front, only in the app after sign-up, and the 'What Athena will not do' disclosure is hidden at the bottom.
findings.expected: Readable text in the demo, and an early statement that this is a demo.
findings.suggested_fix: Scale up the video text for narrow screens. Add a one-line demo notice near the Start button.

findings.what_happened: The paper detail shows 'Contemporary clinical trials · 2025 · ? citations' and the per-query counts show identical numbers for different queries (PubMed 9,245 for two queries, OpenAlex 707 for two). The demo banner appears on every page rather than once as the intent describes.
findings.expected: Hide unknown counts rather than show '?', distinct counts per query, and one dismissible demo note.
findings.suggested_fix: Show 'citations not available' only when needed, make recorded counts distinct, and remember the dismissed banner.

findings.what_happened: Compared with docs/ux-intent.md, steps matched the intended reading and the colour rule ('colours and shapes show kind of study; legend; click to show one kind') was understood. Differences: Step 1 duplicates /s/new; the 'Single next action' on Export is Download but nothing confirms it; demo mode is meant to be announced once and dismissible but returns on each page; the Overview canvas does not highlight the step that needs the user on a phone.
findings.expected: The pages behave as the intent table says.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the Export confirmation, demo-banner persistence, and mobile canvas default with the intent document.

findings.what_happened: The 'supporting quotes' for candidate 2's gap ('the included papers do not measure this link directly') are four green 'found word for word' chips from one paper (Ly et al. 2026). The one I opened is a methods sentence about the Arksey and O'Malley review framework. It says nothing about apps and sugar level. That paper never appeared in my synthesis or appraisal. The same chips are copied into the report as '[Ly et al. 2026]'.
findings.expected: A quote attached to a gap should support that gap, or the page should say that 'found' only means the words exist. The cited paper should be one I appraised, or be clearly marked as not appraised.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a relevance check on each supporting quote and restrict gap citations to appraised papers. Put the 'found does not mean it proves' note next to the chips on the question cards, not only in the popover. Label quotes that are only about methods.

findings.what_happened: The novelty check returned 7,629 PubMed hits for the app-and-sugar-level query. The top OpenAlex hits were unrelated (abortion family planning, retinopathy screening, COVID quarantine). The page gives no plain verdict. There is only a generic note: 'Finding none does not prove a question is new'. The novelty query ignores type 2 diabetes and Thailand, so it does not test my final question. The numbers are hidden inside the collapsed reasoning.
findings.expected: A clear sentence such as 'many similar studies exist, so this is probably not new' or 'search too broad to judge'. The query should match the chosen question.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a one-line novelty summary on each card (for example '7,629 papers match a broad search: this may not be new'). Build the novelty query from all PECO parts. Warn when the top hits do not match the topic.

findings.what_happened: My typos went straight into the work. 'diabtes pateint' became the topic 'Diabetes pateint' and the 'Who' field. The candidate questions read 'type 2 diabetes pateints'. The report title is my raw misspelled sentence. No step offered to correct spelling. I could only fix the topic by noticing it and editing by hand. The title of the final report keeps the typos.
findings.expected: The AI should rewrite my rough, misspelled idea into clean wording and show it for approval. Misspelled search terms hurt the database searches.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Tidy my wording' suggestion in step 2 and use the cleaned idea for topics, candidates and the report title. Flag likely spelling mistakes in topic names.

findings.what_happened: For the topic 'Type 2 diabetes patients' the selected paper #1 was a telemedicine scoping review protocol. Rows #2 to #5 (abortion care, hemophilia care) say both 'does not match the topic' and 'Selected for appraisal in this topic'. The checklist item 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic' showed as Done while the orange banner said 4 topics had fewer than 3. Paper 2 of the appraisal was an HIV study in Malaysia.
findings.expected: Rows that do not match should not carry a 'selected' label. The checklist should not tick when the rule is broken. Irrelevant papers should not move forward silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide or fix the 'Selected for appraisal in this topic' line on non-matching rows. Tie the checklist tick to the real count. Say plainly 'no good papers found for this topic: change the search or drop the topic'.

findings.what_happened: Demo mode is not mentioned on the landing page or the sign-up page. The landing page says 'It finds real papers in PubMed and OpenAlex'. I only learned the AI was scripted and the papers were recorded samples (on telemedicine) after I had created an account and started.
findings.expected: A short demo note before sign-up, so I do not expect results about my topic.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the demo note on the landing and sign-up pages when the server is in demo mode.

findings.what_happened: The password hint 'At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email.' is drawn on top of the password box, inside it, so the field looks like it already has text in it. The Create account button looks active while the form is empty.
findings.expected: The hint should sit below the field, and the button should look clearly disabled or explain what is missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the layout so the hint is below the input. Also check the pages in a narrow window.

findings.what_happened: I had just typed my idea on the first page. The overview then showed 'Your next step: step 1 of 9, Tell us what you want to research', and opening it showed the same idea box again, with a button 'Start scoping'. It felt like I had to repeat step 1. 'Scoping' is a hard word for me.
findings.expected: After I typed my idea, step 1 should count as done and the next step should be the questions.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark step 1 as done on submit and take the user straight to the questions. Use plain wording such as 'Ask me questions'.

findings.what_happened: The scoping questions stopped after 5 and never asked about study types, yet 'What we know so far' ends with 'Which kinds of studies: not answered yet'. The header says 'questions done'. The topic rows are labelled 'Suggested subtopic', a word that never explained itself. A synonym 'if app' appeared next to 'mobile app'. The HbA1c outcome I said I cared about was not turned into a topic, so I had to add it myself. 'Controlled vocabulary (MeSH)' appeared unexplained on the first view, and was explained only on the later screen.
findings.expected: Cover all points or say which I can skip. Use words I know. Offer topics for outcomes I named. Remove junk synonyms.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask about study type or mark it 'optional, skipped'. Rename 'Suggested subtopic' to 'Suggested topic'. Explain MeSH in one line wherever it first appears.

findings.what_happened: The 'Count matches' preview said 979 PubMed papers for the 'Mobile app' query, but after Run the same query showed 8,058. 979 also appears for both 'Type 2 diabetes patients' and 'HbA1c blood sugar control'. The 'Mobile app' query contains 'AND sugar level', so it is not just about apps. The demo note explains some mismatch but not why a preview and a run differ.
findings.expected: A preview count that matches the later run, or a note that says why it can differ.
findings.suggested_fix: Make demo counts consistent, or tag them as demo numbers. Name each query by what it really searches.

findings.what_happened: The header says '6 quotes to decide' while every quote I first saw was green 'found word for word'. I had to find the checkbox 'Show only quotes I need to decide' to see what was meant. The checklist, a long paragraph and a toggle fill more than half of the tablet screen before any paper content appears. Words like 'quality questions' and 'Accept anyway' were hard for me. Many 'found' quotes had little to do with the question (for example the paper title as the quote for 'Random allocation method described').
findings.expected: Show the quotes needing a decision first. Keep the instructions short.
findings.suggested_fix: Turn on 'only quotes I need to decide' by default, or put the items to decide at the top. Shorten the intro and collapse it after the first paper.

findings.what_happened: The 'Known' statement only says '(mock) 6 key findings were extracted for this topic', with chips. It says nothing I could use. The 'conflict' is a sample paired 'at random' and 'They do not necessarily disagree'. After I rejected the altered quotes, the synthesis still listed findings with green ticks, and I could not tell which papers or quotes backed which statement.
findings.expected: A real statement of what is known, tied to specific quotes. A conflict that is really a conflict.
findings.suggested_fix: In real mode, require each statement to quote its source in the text. In demo mode, label the whole block 'example only' prominently, not just with '(mock)'.

findings.what_happened: The focus check reported 'Canvas' with no visible focus style. On the tablet the Canvas view is almost empty because the side panel covers it (only one node visible). Small text and icon-only controls (the 'K' shortcut button, '8 s') are unexplained.
findings.expected: A visible keyboard focus ring everywhere. A useful Canvas view at 768 px, or a hint that it needs a wider screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a focus ring to the Canvas/List toggle. Close the panel by default when opening Canvas on tablets, and label the 'K' shortcut ('Search and commands').

findings.what_happened: I could find and filter by study type and article type and the legend was clear (colour, shape, label, count). A few things confused me. 'Review article 10' (article type) and 'Systematic / scoping review 3' (study type) are different things with similar names. The study-type counts changed between step 4 (Trial 4, Review 3, Other 8, Not reported 49) and step 5 (Cross-sectional 14, Review 7, Not reported 13) with only a short explanation. The key lists categories with no counts (Cohort, Cross-sectional, Qualitative). The 3D chart on tablet is clipped on the right, 'Height has no meaning yet' is odd, and protocols appear as 'Trial' or 'Systematic review' though the intent says protocols are 'Other design'.
findings.expected: Counts that agree across steps, or an explanation next to them. Categories with no papers shown as 0 or hidden.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line explaining article type versus study type. Fix the chart width at 768 px and show 0 for empty categories.

findings.what_happened: The candidate questions keep '(mock)' inside the editable question text, so I had to delete it by hand. Editing the question text left the gap, feasibility and supporting quotes from the original wording, with no warning that they may no longer fit. 'PICo' and 'PECO' are abbreviations I do not know (the brackets help a little). After 'Download the report (Markdown)' I saw no confirmation. 'Markdown, plain text with formatting marks such as #' is jargon for me. 'Open printable report' appeared to open the same page again, and I could not confirm it worked.
findings.expected: Clean editable text, a note after edits, and visible feedback after a download.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip '(mock)' from editable fields. After a wording edit, show 'The gap and quotes were written for the old wording: check them'. Add a 'Downloaded' message. Use 'Report (text file) or printable page' wording.

findings.what_happened: Idioms and technical words for a second-language reader: 'the way you would say it to a supervisor', 'fix any wrong cells', 'Keep', 'found word for word', 'does not match the topic', 'PICo', 'MeSH', 'dupes', '(mock)'. The words mostly became clear from context, and the plain-language notes are a strength. The AI text marked '(mock)' is honest, but it appears inside text I should edit and export.
findings.expected: Short, concrete words wherever possible.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'cells' with 'boxes', 'dupes' with 'duplicates', and add short glosses on first use.

three_second_test.note: I understood it makes a research question from my idea with real papers. 'Start a review' is obvious. I did not see any demo-mode warning here.
It is a simple account form. The password hint overlaps the password box, which is confusing.
A big box for my idea, with examples, and 'Start my review'. Clear.
It showed 'step 1 of 9, Tell us what you want to research' after I had just typed my idea, which made me think I had to do it again. The demo note was clear. The 'K' button was unclear.
One question at a time, in a chat box, with a 'what we know so far' summary. I understood it. The summary showed my typos.
Keep, Edit or Delete for each topic, and the button 'Keep N suggested topics'. 'Suggested subtopic' was confusing.
I saw the searches before they run, plus 'Count matches' and 'Run all 10 searches'. The demo notice is clear. AND/any-of groups are hard but explained.
I saw the paper counts and the study-type bars with colour, shape and label. The 'Summarise the papers' button is clear.
A 3-item checklist, filter chips for study type and article type, and 'Rank the papers'. 'Cells' is spreadsheet jargon.
Lots of text, an orange warning and a checklist that said 'done' for a rule that was broken. It was hard to say what to do first.
Too much instruction text and the real content is below the fold. I did not know what '6 quotes to decide' meant until I turned on the filter.
Tabs by topic, with Known, Contested and Unknown blocks and quote chips. The layout is clear but the statements are vague.
Three cards with gap, feasibility and weakness, and 'Choose this question'. Clear.
The question at the top, three download formats, a preview, and 'Download Markdown'. Clear. The demo label on the report is honest.

reports.categories_and_colours: I could find and filter papers by both dimensions. On Retrieval, the article-type bars are plain grey and tappable, and tapping 'Review article' filtered the chart ('showing 10 of 64'). On the summary table, the chips for study type (colour and shape) and article type (plain) filter the list, with a 'Showing 5 of 64' line and a Reset button. Study types were shown with colour, shape and a text label in the table, chips, map and legend: blue circle for Trial, orange square for Cohort, green triangle for Cross-sectional, amber diamond for Qualitative, pink star for Systematic/scoping review, green cross for Other design and grey ring for Not reported. I understood the meaning without being told because every item has a legend with a label and count. Weak points: two greens (triangle and cross) look similar and only the shape separates them; categories with no papers appear in the key with no count; article type 'Review article' versus study type 'Systematic / scoping review' can be mixed up; counts for the same studies change between step 4 and step 5; the 3D map was clipped on the right at 768 px and 'Height has no meaning yet' is odd.
reports.validity_assessment: Partly valid and honest, but not fully traceable. Strong points: demo mode is announced on every working page, AI text is tagged '(mock)', every paper has DOI/PMID links and its abstract, the scoring rubric (5 criteria and weights) is visible, and the 'Abstract only' badge says what was read. The quote checker works: a deliberately altered quote was shown in red as 'not found, you decide' with the closest passage, and the report counts 54 found, 6 not found, 6 rejected by me. The final report carries a demo disclaimer and a 'not proof of novelty' note, and 'novel' is never claimed. Weak points: 'found word for word' only means the words exist in the paper, and several green quotes were off topic (a paper title as evidence for random allocation; a review-methods sentence as evidence for a research gap). The gap cites a paper I never appraised. The synthesis statements in demo mode are placeholders ('6 key findings were extracted'), so I cannot trace a claim to evidence. The novelty check shows 7,629 hits with no verdict and an unrelated top-hit list. Papers about abortion, hemophilia and HIV were pre-selected for a diabetes topic. My typos flowed into topics, the question and the report title. Nothing looked fabricated in a hidden way: everything off-topic is explained by the demo-mode note. In a real run, I would need the quote relevance and the novelty verdict to be fixed before trusting the report.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I did not quit. The points where a real second-language user might: step 6 Ranking (many words, a contradictory checklist, 4 of 5 topics with fewer than 3 papers) and step 7 Appraisal (long instructions, and the quotes needing a decision hidden behind a toggle).
reports.activity: Created account somchai.nonnative.it2@example.com (name Somchai). Started one project (prj_f950aa1934d24a0e) with the idea 'how mobile app help diabtes pateint in thailand control there sugar level?'. Answered 5 scoping questions. Edited 2 topics, added the topic 'HbA1c blood sugar control', and kept 5 topics. Counted one search and ran all 10 searches (64 unique papers after 55 duplicates removed). Summarised the papers, ranked them, and appraised 6 papers (chose 'Appraise anyway' on the warning). Rejected all 6 'not found' altered quotes. Generated the synthesis and 3 candidate questions, chose candidate 2, and edited its wording and population. Reached the export page and previewed the report (457 lines), clicked 'Download the report (Markdown)' and opened the CSV option. About 115 helper commands. No console errors or failed requests were reported by 'problems' at any step. My own ambiguous click targets ('Add', 'Candidate 2') triggered the wrong controls at times; I recovered each time.
reports.narrative: I opened the landing page and understood within a few seconds that Athena turns a rough idea into a research question with real papers. I signed up (the password hint sat on top of the password box, which looked odd) and typed my sentence with its typos. The session page then asked me again to 'Tell us what you want to research', which confused me for a moment. The demo-mode note was clear and honest, although I wish I had seen it before signing up. Scoping was easy: five short questions in plain English. But my typo 'diabtes pateint' turned into a search topic and I fixed it by hand. The searches page was good: the demo note explained that the counts are recorded samples. The retrieval and table pages were the best part for me. The study-type colours, shapes and counts were consistent, and I could filter by study type and by article type. The ranking page was the first place I felt lost: an orange warning, a checklist that said 'done' while the warning said otherwise, and papers about abortion for a diabetes topic. The appraisal page was heavy on text, but the red 'not found, you decide' card for an altered quote showed that the quote check is real. I rejected those quotes. The synthesis was vague ('6 key findings were extracted'), though the quote popover was good. At the final step I chose the association question, and it still had typos and '(mock)' in it, so I rewrote it. The export page was clear, and the report is labelled as a demo. I would trust the process more than the content until the novelty check and quote relevance improve.

findings.what_happened: On the table and ranking pages the primary button (Rank the papers / Appraise selected papers) is a sticky bar, but in the keyboard order it comes after every paper row. I counted about 95 Tab presses from the page heading to reach it. There is no 'Skip to the next action' link on these full pages (the side panels have one), and Skip to content only jumps to the top.
findings.expected: A keyboard user can reach the single primary action in a few keystrokes, as in the step panels with 'Skip to the next action'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Skip to the next action' and 'Skip the table' links at the top of /table. Make table rows a single tab stop with arrow-key navigation (grid pattern), or put the primary action early in the tab order.

findings.page: All step panels, topic edit, overview
findings.what_happened: Focus is lost or jumps unpredictably after many actions. It falls to the page body after closing a panel with Esc, after hiding the demo note, after the page changes to /table or /export, and after Keep on a list row. It is sent back to the panel heading after Reject on a quote, after Count matches, after Choose this question and after saving a synonym. Pressing Esc inside the 'Edit statement' textarea on the synthesis step closed the whole panel and returned focus to the body, not just the edit.
findings.expected: After an action, focus stays on or returns to the control that triggered it, or moves to a clearly announced place. Esc cancels only the innermost edit.
findings.suggested_fix: Return focus to the opener on panel close. Keep focus on the next undecided quote after Accept or Reject. Make Esc close the edit first. Move focus to the new page's h1 on navigation.

findings.what_happened: At step 3 I changed the synonyms of the first topic. The panel silently turned into 'Edit this search topic' (Step 2 of 9, Your turn), the whole review went back to step 2, and all 5 topics showed 'Your turn' again. There was no message saying that my edit invalidated the approval. I had to re-open step 2 and re-approve. Focus also jumped to the heading when I tabbed out of the MeSH field.
findings.expected: A clear 'You changed a topic, so the earlier approval is out of date. Keep or bring up to date' message, and the step view stays where I was.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the stated 'out of date' state with the reason and a Keep or Bring up to date choice, as the UX intent describes. Do not swap the panel content without explanation.

findings.page: Demo mode: ranking, appraisal, synthesis, report
findings.what_happened: The topic returned irrelevant sample papers (a Ramadan diabetes trial, hemophilia in Southeast Asia, telemedicine in Makassar). Eight of them went forward to appraisal. The synthesis had one paper for 'Peer support groups', and 'Postpartum depression' and 'Mothers' had no tab at all. The demo-mode note appears only once on the overview and is dismissible. I dismissed it by keyboard, and it did not appear again on /table, the ranking page or the synthesis. Landing and signup never mention demo mode. The report does carry an honest 'Demo: ... not a real review' line and a '(mock)' prefix on the chosen question.
findings.expected: A first-time visitor learns before signing up that this is a demo with sample papers. The reminder stays visible wherever papers and scores are shown, and cannot be lost by one keypress.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a persistent small 'Demo data' badge in the header on every step and full page. Mention demo mode on the landing page and signup. Make the dismissed note re-openable.

findings.what_happened: At 200% zoom the hint 'At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email.' is drawn on top of the Password input and overlaps its bottom border. The visible label order is awkward (Email label sits directly under the Name field with no gap). Email is auto-focused, skipping the optional name field, and the empty field has no accessible name.
findings.expected: The hint sits below the field with space, and every input has an accessible name.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the layout of the helper text (static flow below the input, margin). Associate the labels and hint with aria-labelledby and aria-describedby.

findings.what_happened: At 200% zoom the panel scroll area is only about 350 to 400 px tall because the header, stepper, sticky footer and the demo note take the rest. The focused heading is cut off at the top after some actions. The scoping answer textarea is half hidden behind the footer. The focus ring of filter chips on /table is partly covered by the sticky header (focus obscured).
findings.expected: The focused element is fully visible, and a reasonable content area remains at 200% zoom.
findings.suggested_fix: Add scroll-padding-top and scroll-padding-bottom equal to the sticky bars. Collapse the stepper and 'Next:' line at narrow effective widths. Make the footer non-sticky at 200% zoom.

findings.page: Scoping topics list, quote list, synthesis
findings.what_happened: Repeated buttons have no unique accessible names: 'Edit', 'Keep' and 'Delete' per topic row, and 'Show source' and 'Pin to canvas' per quote. A keyboard or screen-reader user hears 'Edit' ten times without knowing which topic. The always-boxed 'Keep' buttons look like they already have focus and can be confused with the real focus ring.
findings.expected: Names such as 'Edit topic Mothers' and 'Show source for quote: Clear statement of aims'. The focus ring is clearly different from the button border.
findings.suggested_fix: Add aria-label with the topic or question name. Restyle 'Keep' so its border is not the same weight as the focus ring.

findings.what_happened: The 3D chart is the default view. Its points cannot be reached or read by keyboard. The legend filter works by keyboard and the '2D chart' toggle is reachable, but the instructions still say 'Click or tap', 'Drag to turn, scroll to zoom' and 'hover or focus ... click'. Even the 2D points are not focusable. Legend entries with 0 papers are dimmed but still tab stops with no explanation.
findings.expected: A keyboard path to the papers behind each point (the table is the equivalent). Keyboard-neutral wording. 2D is the default when focus-visible or reduced motion is used.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword instructions to 'Press Enter or click'. Default to 2D for keyboard users or on request. Link to the table as the accessible alternative. Mark zero-count legend items as 'none'.

findings.what_happened: The scripted AI produced awkward topics and synonyms: 'Postpartum depressive' as a topic, and 'whether groups' as a synonym for peer support groups (taken from my outcome answer). The 'What we know so far' header says 'questions done' with no number. Question text starts with '(mock)'. The study-type question is never asked, so the report says 'studyTypes: (mock) Any design'.
findings.expected: Synonyms are meaningful terms, counters show a number ('5 of 5 questions done'), and unanswered fields are not presented as if answered.
findings.suggested_fix: Fill in the count. Validate synonyms against the topic. Show unanswered criteria as 'not set' in the report.

findings.page: Topic edit panel ('Keep or delete this suggested topic')
findings.what_happened: The heading says 'Keep or delete' but the buttons say 'Dismiss' and 'Keep this topic'. After 'Keep this topic' the app opens another panel ('Edit this search topic') that I did not ask for, and the kept topic still shows 'Your turn' with 0 MeSH.
findings.expected: Consistent wording (Delete versus Dismiss) and a stay-where-I-am result after Keep.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to 'Keep or dismiss', or the button to 'Delete'. After Keep, return to the list with a confirmation.

findings.what_happened: After typing my idea on /s/new, the overview still says 'Your next step: Tell us what you want to research' and 'Draft idea', and I had to open step 1 and press 'Start scoping' to continue. 'What happens in this step 8 s' reads like a loading time. The 'Do these things' lists say 'Click' throughout, even though 'Enter on it' is mentioned once.
findings.expected: The step after submitting the idea is step 2. '8 s' is labelled as a video length.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the explainer 'Video, 8 s'. Make Start my review go straight to the scoping questions or explain the extra step.

findings.what_happened: Quotes are marked 'found word for word' even when they are just the paper title or a section label ('TITLE Clinicians perceptions...') used as evidence for 'Clear statement of aims' with the AI answer 'Unclear'. One quote is a deliberately altered test item ('(mock) Paraphrase presented as a quote — should be flagged') which is honestly flagged 'not found, you decide', with the closest passage shown (54% match). The app says plainly that 'found' does not mean 'proves'. 9 quotes needed a decision, and leaving them undecided drops them from the synthesis with only a footnote and a confirmation dialog.
findings.expected: The check should not count a title or heading as supporting evidence, and the leftover undecided quotes should be easy to resolve.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude title and heading text from quote matching. Add 'Accept all found, decide the rest' navigation and keep focus on the next undecided quote.

findings.what_happened: 'Open printable report' opens in a new tab with no warning, and the helper could not follow it. The download link gives a polite status message ('Downloading the report (Markdown). It will be in your browser's downloads.') but that makes the preview jump down. The report preview is a focusable scroll box, which works well, and the report notes quotes found 77, not found 9, undecided 8, and that novelty hits are 'not proof of novelty'. The chosen research question still starts with '(mock)'.
findings.expected: New-tab links are announced, and the layout does not shift on download.
findings.suggested_fix: Add '(opens in a new tab)' to the link text. Reserve space for the status message.

findings.what_happened: The checklist says 'Read each topic, and its 2 conflicts' but the visible 'Contested' list for Peer support groups says 'Nothing identified'. Only three of the five topics have tabs.
findings.expected: Counts in the checklist match what is shown, and topics with no evidence are listed as 'no papers'.
findings.suggested_fix: Show empty topics as tabs marked 'no evidence'. Word the checklist by the current tab.

findings.what_happened: '(mock)' prefixes appear inside every key-finding cell, paper summary and candidate question, which makes text noisy at 200% zoom and lengthens the screen reader output.
findings.expected: Demo status is shown once per page (badge), not repeated in every sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a demo badge and strip the repeated '(mock)' prefix from the UI text, keeping it in the exported report if needed.

three_second_test.note: Purpose (idea to research question with real papers) was clear from the headline. First action: Start a review. Next: sign up. Tab order is Skip, Log in, Start a review, I have an account, with a visible ring. Nothing here says it is a demo.
Create an account. Email is auto-focused. Next: password, Create account. The hint overlapping the password box at 200% zoom was distracting.
Describe the idea in a sentence, then Start my review. Textarea was focused, example chips were reachable by Tab.

I expected to be in the questions already. The page showed 'Your next step: Tell us what you want to research' for something I had just typed. The primary action 'Open step 1' was clear only after reading.
Answer five short questions; 'Skip the rest' is available. The answer box is half hidden at 200% zoom.
Keep, edit or delete each suggested topic, or 'Keep 5 suggested topics'. Focus landed on the footer button and I did not see the heading.
Check the searches then 'Run all 10 searches'. The demo notice explains that the searches are a recorded example.
'134 results fetched, 37 duplicates, 97 different papers' is plain. Article type and study type facets are clear. The 3D chart default is not usable by keyboard.
Skim papers and correct cells, then Rank. The three-item checklist helped. The Rank button was far down the tab order.
Scores of 34 out of 100 and an unrelated diabetes trial at the top made me doubt it. The 3 topic warning dialog helped.
Go paper by paper, check quotes, decide the red 'not found' ones. 'found word for word' with a tick and 'not found' with a cross are clear without colour.
Known, Contested, Unknown with quote chips. Topic tabs worked with arrow keys. Checklist counts did not match what was shown.
Three candidates with gap, feasibility, weakness, then Choose this question. 'Finish and export' stays locked with a reason until I choose.
Pick a format and download. The report preview, the demo line and the quote counts were all visible.

reports.categories_and_colours: I found study type and article type filters on the Retrieval page (chips and chart legend) and on the table page (chip rows, 'More filters', a Group by select). Study type shows a coloured shape plus a text label plus a count: Trial is a blue circle, Cohort/case-control an orange square, Cross-sectional a green triangle, Qualitative/mixed a gold diamond, Systematic/scoping a pink star, Other design a green cross, Not reported a grey ring. Article types (Journal article, Review article, Preprint, Editorial/letter/comment) have no colour or shape, only text and count. Both filter by keyboard (Enter on a chip). The app says 'Showing 5 of 97: trial. 92 papers are hidden by your filters (still in the review)' with a Reset filters button, so it is not misleading. Counts are consistent (97 papers). The earlier retrieval page says Not reported 80 versus 17 in the table after AI summaries, and the app explains this. The legend text was understandable without being told, and selected chips show a check mark. One issue is that zero-count legend entries are dimmed but still focusable with no explanation, and the 3D points cannot be reached by keyboard.
reports.validity_assessment: The app is mostly honest in demo mode: a banner says the AI is scripted and papers are samples, the search builder says the searches are 'a recorded example, not built from your topics', candidate questions say 'Demo mode searches recorded sample papers on telemedicine, so few will match your topic', and the report opens with 'Demo: ... not a real review'. The workflow design is traceable: every statement links to a quote chip, 'Show source' highlights the quote in the retrieved text, fabricated quotes are flagged as 'not found, you decide' with the closest passage, 'found' is explained as 'in the paper, not proof', the novelty check says 'finding none does not prove a question is new', and the report lists the counts of found, not found, accepted, rejected and undecided quotes. Weak points: (1) the demo note is dismissible and not repeated where the papers are ranked; landing and signup do not mention demo at all; (2) 'found word for word' is satisfied by titles and section labels; (3) irrelevant papers (diabetes, hemophilia) were ranked top for a postpartum depression topic, and two of five topics had zero papers, yet the chosen question is still produced and the report is called 'ready'. Nothing looked fabricated beyond the labelled mock content. In a real run the same structure would give a traceable review.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I did not quit. The point where a keyboard-only user would most likely give up is the summary table and ranking pages: about 95 Tab stops to reach 'Rank the papers' or 'Appraise selected papers', with no skip link, plus focus resets to the body after panel closes and after each quote decision (9 decisions, each sending focus back to the top).
reports.activity: Created one account (ruth.lecturer.test@example.com) and one project (prj_824dbdb9ec9d47c1) on the topic 'Peer support groups for postpartum depression in low-income countries'. I answered all 5 scoping questions, kept 5 topics (edited one name and one synonym list, which sent the review back to step 2 so I re-approved), wrote and ran 10 searches (97 unique papers from 134 results), summarised 97 papers, ranked, appraised 8 papers anyway after a 3-topic warning, rejected 1 quote and left 8 undecided, summarised the evidence anyway after a second warning, suggested 3 research questions, chose candidate 2 (PECO association question), and reached Export. I opened the report preview and clicked 'Download the report (Markdown)', which showed a 'downloading' status. No console errors or failed requests were reported at any step. I did not open the Map view, Account, command palette or Admin. Screenshots are 01 to 54 in docs/qa/iteration-2/keyboard/.
reports.narrative:
I started at 200% zoom with only the keyboard. The landing page told me quickly what Athena is for, and Tab showed a bold ring on each control, which was a relief. Sign-up worked, but the hint under the password box was printed over the box. I typed my topic and answered the five scoping questions, and the app moved focus to the panel heading each time a step changed, which helps. The panel content area is small at 200% zoom, so I often scrolled to find the input.

I lost orientation several times. After closing a panel, hiding the demo note, or opening the table page, focus fell back to the top of the page. Changing one synonym at step 3 quietly sent the whole review back to step 2 and I had no idea why until I read the list. On the table page I needed about 95 Tab presses to reach the Rank button, and I wished for a skip link.

The study type and article type filters were good: shape, colour and text together, counts, a clear 'hidden by your filters' message and a Reset button. The 3D chart was no use by keyboard, but the 2D toggle and the legend worked.

I was pleased by the honest parts: the demo banner, the warning dialogs, the red 'not found, you decide' quotes with Show source, and the novelty caveat. Still, the top-ranked papers were about diabetes and hemophilia, two topics had no papers, and yet I got a tidy research question and a finished report. I would have trusted it more if the demo reminder stayed on every screen. I reached Export, read the preview, and downloaded the Markdown report.

findings.what_happened: The novelty check box says 'No closely matching records were returned. This does not prove the question is new.' directly under 'pubmed: 2,207 matching records / openalex: 412 matching records'. The exported report repeats '2207 hits' and '412 hits' for the exact query. The two statements contradict each other. The 2,207 figure is the same recorded count shown earlier for a different query (step 3), so it is not even the count for this question.
findings.expected: A novelty check whose headline agrees with its numbers. If hundreds or thousands of records match, say 'many records match, check them'. In demo mode, label the counts as sample numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Show how many hits were close matches and how many are just keyword hits. Do not print 'no closely matching records' when the hit count is above 0 unless the close-match rule is explained. Tag demo counts '(sample)'.

findings.page: Report preview / Scoping section of exported report
findings.what_happened: I skipped scoping questions 4 and 5 (years, kinds of studies) with 'Skip the rest'. The report's Scoping section still lists 'timeframe: (mock) 2015 onwards' and 'studyTypes: (mock) Any design' as if I had answered them. The 'What we know so far' panel had said 'not answered yet' for both.
findings.expected: Unanswered fields stay 'not answered' or are marked 'assumed by Athena', so a supervisor reading the report does not think the student chose them.
findings.evidence: docs/qa/iteration-2/chaos/09-topics.jpg (not answered yet) vs docs/qa/iteration-2/chaos/58-preview.jpg (timeframe 2015 onwards, studyTypes Any design)
findings.suggested_fix: Label values the user did not give as 'default, not chosen by you'. Or list them under 'Assumptions'.

findings.what_happened: The checklist item 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic' was ticked as Done, and struck through, while the amber warning on the same page said 3 of 4 topics had fewer than 3 papers (2, 0 and 0). Appraising then opened a dialog saying '3 topics have fewer than 3 papers'. The page contradicts itself before I click.
findings.expected: The item stays unticked while any topic has fewer than 3 selected papers.
findings.suggested_fix: Tick the item only when every topic has 3-5 selected papers or the user has pressed 'Appraise anyway'.

findings.what_happened: The top-ranked paper for the topic 'Short-form video apps' is 'A holistic lifestyle mobile health intervention for ... type 2 diabetes ... Asian women' with score 65, and it is ticked 'Keep'. Nothing on the row says it is off-topic. The text says 'papers that match the topic' are selected. Some topics list 'Measurement and outcomes: 4 selected' although the map legend showed 0 papers for that topic. Demo mode explains why topics do not match, but the ranking numbers look real.
findings.expected: A paper with no mention of the topic should not look like a match. In demo mode the score column should say 'sample'. Topic counts should agree between the chart legend and the topic buttons.
findings.evidence: docs/qa/iteration-2/chaos/35-rank-table-view.jpg ; docs/qa/iteration-2/chaos/26-2d-topic.jpg (Measurement and outcomes has no count) vs docs/qa/iteration-2/chaos/32-rank.jpg (4 selected)
findings.suggested_fix: Show a 'why it matched' line and a low-relevance warning. Make the per-topic counts come from one source. Add a visible '(sample score)' tag in demo mode.

findings.what_happened: Count matches for topic 1 showed 'PubMed 2,207'. After 'Run all 8 searches', the same query card said 'PubMed 9,245'. The topics 'Short-form video apps' and 'Measurement and outcomes' also show identical counts (9,245 and 50) and the first of them owns 67 of the 110 papers while the second owns none. The page warns that only the 40 most relevant are collected, but not that the number changes.
findings.expected: The same query shows the same count before and after running, or says why it changed.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the preview count and the run count separately and label them. In demo mode say 'recorded sample counts'.

findings.page: Topic edit panel (Edit this search topic)
findings.what_happened: I changed the topic name Teenagers to 'Adolescents aged 13-17' and pressed Tab. The 'Edit an earlier step?' dialog came up. I pressed Cancel. The panel field still showed 'Adolescents aged 13-17', but the canvas card still said 'Teenagers', and after a reload the field was back to 'Teenagers'. The panel looked as if the edit had been saved.
findings.expected: Cancel puts the old value back in the field.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset the field to the saved value when the dialog is cancelled.

findings.what_happened: A paper shows the green 'Full text' badge and 'Read on the open full text'. The 'Show source' view then displays text that starts 'TITLE ... ABSTRACT BACKGROUND', which looks like title plus abstract only. The wording 'Only the abstract could be read' appears on another paper. The 'Aim' field is the raw title and abstract text pasted in. The line 'Paper 1 of 6 ... 8 quotes to decide' counts all papers, while the checklist for paper 1 says 'Nothing to decide'.
findings.expected: The badge matches what the source viewer shows. Counts say 'across all 6 papers'.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the real source length under the badge. Say 'in all papers' next to the undecided count.

findings.what_happened: Mouse-wheel scrolling over the 3D chart zooms the chart instead of scrolling the page. In the ranking Map view there is nothing below the chart (no table), so the page seemed to end. 'Showing all 67' appears above a chart that shows only about 6 clear dots; the faded dots are almost invisible. The chart's colour meaning changes with the 'Colour by' choice (blue = Trial in one view, blue = Short-form video apps in another), and the choice is kept between steps, so I opened the map in step 5 already coloured by Topic.
findings.expected: Page scroll still works over the chart (zoom only after a click or with Ctrl). The map should say that the table is under the Table tab. The legend should say which dimension is active.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not capture the wheel until the chart has focus. Make faded dots at least 30 percent visible. Reset 'Colour by' to Study type on each step or show the active dimension in the heading.

findings.what_happened: Study-type chips and article-type chips combine as AND. I picked Trial (6) then Review article (11) and got 'Showing 0 of 110'. The chip counts did not change after the first click, so I could not tell the combination was empty before clicking it. The empty state and 'Reset filters' link are clear.
findings.expected: After one filter is on, the other chips show how many papers remain (for example 'Review article 0').
findings.suggested_fix: Update chip counts to reflect the active filters, and grey out chips that would give 0.

findings.what_happened: A paper labelled 'Trial / Randomised trial' is a study protocol (title says 'protocol'), and its Key finding is just '(mock) NCT07198828.' - a registry number, not a finding. A protocol has no results, yet it is counted under 'Trial' beside completed trials. Other design includes 'protocols' only according to the intent doc; this one was filed as Trial.
findings.expected: Protocols are not counted as trials with findings. The key finding column says 'No results yet (protocol)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Detect 'protocol' in the title or abstract and file it under Other design. Reject registry IDs as key findings.

findings.what_happened: The gap statement in the report cites [Sujarwoto et al. 2022; Godinho et al. 2020], but the candidate card in the app cited 'Lee et al. 2015 limitation' and the synthesis cites only Lee 2015 and Salamanca-Sanabria 2024. I could not tell which papers support the gap. The cards also use 'PECO' and 'PICo' without explaining them, and show raw search strings like [tiab] in the novelty box.
findings.expected: The same citations in the app and the report. Plain-word names for frameworks, with the raw queries behind a Details link.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate both from one data source. Add a one-line gloss: 'PECO = Population, Exposure, Comparison, Outcome'. Collapse raw queries.

findings.what_happened: The chosen question keeps its '(mock)' prefix in the 'Your research question' box and in the report. That is honest, but a student copying it has to delete it by hand. The format cards have clumsy wording ('Markdown, plain text with formatting marks such as # for headings'). 'Open printable report' did not visibly change the page in my browser; it probably opens a new tab, which I could not see, so I could not check the printed layout. The download message 'It will be in your browser's downloads' gave me no file name.
findings.expected: A clear way to export the question without '(mock)' text, and visible feedback when the printable report opens.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'Report (Markdown, for editors)' and 'Printable report (opens in a new tab)'. Show the file name after download.

findings.what_happened: On the first canvas the idea card offered 'Sharpen my idea' and the banner above offered 'Open step 1 - Tell us what you want to research', although I had just written my idea. Two buttons, and the second's text sounded like I had to do it again. Pressing 'Sharpen my idea' marked step 1 as Approved without a confirm step.
findings.expected: One primary action. The banner text should say 'Next: answer a few questions'.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide the 'Your next step' banner when the card already has a button, or reword it to match the button.

findings.what_happened: The canvas cards say 'Accept' and 'Dismiss', while the panel says 'Keep' and 'Delete'. The editor shows 'Controlled vocabulary (MeSH)' with the value 'none' and no explanation until a later note ('PubMed's official keywords'). The step labels also disagree: the stepper calls step 2 'Scoping', the landing page calls step 2 'Turn it into search topics'. A '8 s' badge on 'What happens in this step' looks like a timer for the step.
findings.expected: One verb pair, one label for each step, and a plain-word hint for MeSH.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Keep / Delete on both. Rename the label to 'Video 8 s'. Add a hint 'Official PubMed subject terms (optional)'.

findings.what_happened: The password hint 'At least 10 characters, not containing the name part of your email' overlaps the bottom edge of the password input, so the box looks cut. The 'Create account' button looks disabled with an empty form and could not be clicked; with a short password the only error was 'Use at least 10 characters.' with no mention that the name rule also applies.
findings.expected: Hint below the input, not inside it. A button that is not allowed to submit explains why.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the label and hint layout. Keep the button enabled and show field errors on submit.

findings.what_happened: The three format cards are buttons that act as radios. When I focused one, the focus tool reported 'NO visible focus style'. Links and the Download button did show an outline.
findings.expected: A visible focus ring on every control for keyboard users.
findings.suggested_fix: Add :focus-visible styling to the format cards.

findings.what_happened: Privacy works: I saw only 'Could not open this session / Project not found' with buttons 'Try again' and 'All sessions'. It shows nothing about the owner or the project. But the page has no Athena header, sits unstyled at the top of the screen, and 'Try again' is pointless for a missing project. The console logged three 404 errors. The wording says 'session' while the app calls them 'projects'. A made-up URL (/nonsense) gives a bright white default 404 with no link back, jarring against the dark app.
findings.expected: A branded, centred message that says 'This project does not exist or is not yours' and links to My projects.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide 'Try again' on 404 and give both error pages the standard header and dark theme.

findings.what_happened: An unsent answer typed into the box was lost when I reloaded. The answers I had already sent were kept. The Back button from inside a project panel took me out of the project to My projects rather than closing the panel. The demo banner returns after every reload although the intent says 'announced once'.
findings.expected: Draft text kept (or a note that it is not saved). Back closes the panel first.
findings.suggested_fix: Save drafts in session storage. Push panel opens onto browser history. Remember the banner dismissal.

reports.categories_and_colours: Study type and article type are easy to find and filter. Step 4 shows two bar lists (article type, study type) with counts. Step 5 and 6 have chip rows 'Study type' and 'Article type' with counts, a 'Group by' menu, and a Table / Map switch. Clicking a chip filters, shows 'Showing X of Y: ...' and a 'hidden by your filters' warning with Reset filters. Chips from the two rows combine as AND and the counts do not update, so a Trial + Review article pick gave 0 papers with no warning beforehand. Colour and shape: study type uses blue circle = Trial, red square = Cohort, green triangle = Cross-sectional, amber diamond = Qualitative, pink star = Systematic review, green cross = Other design, grey ring = Not reported. Every legend entry carries both a shape and a text label with a count, and the legend says 'hover or focus to highlight, click to show only that category'. I understood it without being told. Issues: (1) 'Other design' and 'Trial' blues and greens are close in the small 3D chart; (2) the same blue means Trial in one 'Colour by' setting and Short-form video apps in another, and the setting persisted between steps, so I opened the step 5 map already coloured by Topic; (3) topic counts in the legend (67 / 4 / 39 / none) do not match the 'selected' counts on the topic buttons in step 6; (4) the 3D chart is cramped, wheel-scroll gets caught by it, and on the ranking map the faded (not selected) dots are hard to see; (5) retrieval-step study-type counts (Not reported 97) change to (Not reported 15) in step 5 after AI reading, which the text explains ('the AI reads every abstract in the next step').
reports.validity_assessment: Traceability is the app's strength. Every appraisal quote carries 'found word for word' or 'not found, you decide', and 'Show source' highlights the exact words in the retrieved text. The app caught a deliberately altered quote ('...clearly proves the intervention works everywhere'), flagged it, let me reject it, and kept it out of the synthesis; the report counts found 61, accepted 0, rejected 1, undecided 7. Wording is careful: 'found means the words are in the paper, not that they prove the answer'; 'the novelty check ... finding none does not prove a question is new'; the abstract-only limit is stated. Demo mode is honest and repeated: a banner on every page, '(mock)' on all AI text, a note that the sample papers are about telemedicine in Southeast Asia, 'Demo: not a real review' at the top of the report, and sample conflict text that says 'They do not necessarily disagree'. I saw nothing invented without a label. Weaknesses that could mislead a real user: the novelty box says no close matches next to thousands of hits, and the report repeats the counts; unanswered scoping fields (years, study types) appear as filled-in values in the report; the ranking shows scores and 'matches' for clearly off-topic papers and ticks 'keep 3-5 papers per topic' when it is not true; the gap citations differ between the app and the report; protocols are counted as trials with 'findings'. I could not test the real AI or real databases, so I cannot say whether the review would be valid outside demo mode. Privacy check: another person's project URL returned only 'Project not found', with no title, owner or step; /admin sent me to my own project list.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I would not have quit. The closest I came was step 6 (Ranking): the top paper was about diabetes in Asian women, the page said 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic' was done while a warning said 0 selected for two topics, and my whole review had 6 papers from unrelated fields. In demo mode I accepted that because the banner explains it. A real student on a real run might quit there if the matches were this poor with no 'why' line.
reports.activity: Created one account (leo.chaos@example.com, name Leo). One failed sign-up attempt with a 6-character password (error: use at least 10 characters), then a successful one. Created one project, 'Effects of short-form video apps on attention span in teenagers' (prj_9fbb4af6531e4844) and ran it from step 1 to the finished export (all 9 steps done). Answered 3 scoping questions and used 'Skip the rest'. Edited one topic's synonyms and kept 4 topics. Wrote the searches, ran count matches once and ran all 8 searches (110 papers, 120 duplicates merged). Summarised the papers, ranked, and appraised 6 papers (accepted the 'fewer than 3 papers' warning). Rejected 1 unverified quote and left 7 undecided, then summarised without them. Chose research question candidate 2. Previewed the report (464 lines), previewed the CSV, and clicked 'Download the report (Markdown)'. Disruptive actions: double-clicked Send answer, Suggest search topics, Start my review and Run all 8 searches (the second click was ignored each time); reloaded mid-scoping, during query writing, and during appraisal; pressed Back inside the project (went to My projects); abandoned the project and reopened it from the list; opened another user's project URL (Project not found); tried /admin (redirected to My projects) and /nonsense (white 404); edited an approved step's topic and cancelled the 'Edit an earlier step?' dialog. Errors seen: a 400 after the weak password, and three 404 console errors on the other user's project page. 'problems' reported no errors on the main flow. All jobs finished almost instantly (mock), so I never saw a long-running state. About 125 helper commands. Browser stopped.
reports.narrative: I landed on Athena and got it straight away: a guided way to turn a rough idea into a research question. I clicked Start a review, signed up, and tried a short password first. The Create account button looked disabled when the form was empty, and the hint text sat on the border of the password box. I typed my topic and double-clicked Start my review; nothing broke. On the first canvas I hesitated, because Sharpen my idea and Open step 1 - Tell us what you want to research seemed to ask the same thing twice. The scoping chat was fine: I answered three questions, reloaded and lost one unsent answer, then skipped the rest. I edited a topic's synonyms, added TikTok and Reels, and kept the topics. The demo banner told me the papers would be about telemedicine, so I was not surprised when 110 papers arrived about Malaysia and Indonesia. I pressed Back and landed on My projects, tried the other person's URL and saw only Project not found, which is good, then reopened my project. In the table I filtered by study type and article type. Combining Trial with Review article gave 0 with no warning in the counts. The ranking page was my low point: Keep 3-5 papers per topic was ticked while the warning said two topics had 0 papers. The appraisal page impressed me: it caught a doctored quote and let me reject it. I edited an approved topic, saw the Edit an earlier step dialog, cancelled, and the field still showed my unsaved text. I chose a question, saw the novelty box say no close matches under 2,207 matching records, and exported the report. Everything finished in under a second, so I never saw progress states.

findings.page: Admin dashboard, scoping step while AI is off (user view, 4102)
findings.what_happened: With AI off, the scoping panel still says 'Answer in your own words, or skip any time'. The answer box is disabled ('Waiting for the next question...') and there is no visible Skip button. The Idea card keeps the orange 'Your turn' badge and '0 of 5 questions' even though nothing can be done. The only guidance is the amber note and 'The first question appears when AI is available again'.
findings.expected: While AI is paused the step shows 'Waiting', not 'Your turn'. The 'skip any time' promise is either removed or the Skip control stays usable. The panel offers one clear thing to do (wait, or come back later).
findings.suggested_fix: When paused, change the badge to 'Waiting for AI'. Hide or reword the 'skip any time' sentence. Tell the user they can close the tab and the step will continue by itself.

findings.page: Admin dashboard, AI & API key panel and Models row
findings.what_happened: In mock mode the key panel shows a masked key ending ••••[last 4 redacted] 'From the server environment (XAI_API_KEY)', with active Test key and Set a key buttons. The same key tail is shown on all 7 servers. The Models row says 'mock · mock · mock' but the cost-by-model table lists 'grok-4.3' and 'grok-4.20-0309-reasoning' with call counts. findings.evidence: docs/qa/iteration-2/admin/05-dash-4101-top.jpg, docs/qa/iteration-2/admin/11-models.jpg and the Cost by model text on every server

findings.what_happened: The green banner repeats itself: heading 'Everything is healthy' and then 'Everything is healthy. Mock mode: nothing is spent.' The reason line adds nothing beyond the mock-mode note. On every healthy server the top 3 seconds say the same thing, which is good, but the repeated words look like a template glitch.
findings.expected: One verdict plus one distinct reason line, for example 'Everything is healthy' then 'Demo mode: AI is scripted and nothing is spent. 0 errors in the last hour.'
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the duplicated 'Everything is healthy.' from the reason sentence.

findings.page: Admin dashboard, AI calls tile and Validation retries tile
findings.what_happened: After the AI-off test the AI calls tile says '1 blocked, not sent' while the Validation retries line says '1 paused'. The same event appears under two different names. The blocked count is correct: AI calls stayed at 48 while AI was off, and rose to 50 only after AI was switched back on. The tile's added line makes the card taller than its neighbours.
findings.expected: One name for one event, 'blocked (AI off)', in both places.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same word in both places and keep the tiles the same height.

findings.page: Admin dashboard, Accounts table versus Audit log
findings.what_happened: The Audit log masks emails (p•••@example.com) but the Accounts table directly above shows full emails. The 'Where people stop' and Users and progress sections correctly show counts only, with no ideas, papers, notes or keys. No email appears in any URL (the page is just /admin). A full email in a table for an admin is probably acceptable, but the masking is inconsistent.
findings.expected: Either mask emails consistently or say on the page why admins see them in Accounts (needed to disable or reset an account).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line note under Accounts ('Emails are shown so you can manage accounts; they are masked in the log'), or show a short form with the full email on hover or in the actions menu.

findings.page: Admin dashboard, security and audit coverage (4107)
findings.what_happened: The chaos user reported a rejected weak-password signup, a non-admin visit to /admin and a visit to another user's project URL, which gave three 404s. None of these show in the audit log, which only lists signup, login ok, admin bootstrapped and the AI on/off changes. It says '0 failed logins in the last 24 h', which is true. Server errors read 0%, which is also true because these are 4xx responses.
findings.expected: An admin might want a line for 'blocked access to another user's project' or 'non-admin tried /admin' in the security log, or a count of 4xx responses.
findings.suggested_fix: Log forbidden and not-found access to other users' projects and non-admin /admin attempts as 'security' events, and show a '4xx (client)' count beside Server errors.
